title: [WebSocket] CONNECT tunnel logic is duplicated in ProxyTunnelConnector and RawSocketTransport and handles a non-reusable 407 differently
body:
## Summary
ProxyTunnelConnector (WebSocket.Transport) and RawSocketTransport.EstablishConnectTunnelAsync each implement the CONNECT write, reply read, challenge check and one Basic retry. The copies differ in how they treat a 407 that closes the connection or has a chunked body, so the WebSocket copy fails where the HTTP transport succeeds. Users connecting wss:// through an authenticating proxy that closes after the first 407 are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:23`

## Problem
ProxyTunnelConnector.EstablishAsync (ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:23-139) and RawSocketTransport.EstablishConnectTunnelAsync (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1428-1516) both write CONNECT, read through ConnectReplyReader, check AuthChallengeParser.OffersScheme and retry once with Basic. They differ: the WebSocket copy sends `Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive` (:150) where HTTP sends `Connection: keep-alive` (:1536); the consent flag is AllowCleartext vs AllowPlaintextProxyAuth; and when the 407 cannot be answered on the same connection the HTTP copy returns null so the caller retries on a fresh connection (:1482-1483) while the WebSocket copy throws ProxyTunnelFailed ('This stack works on a single stream', :118-126). Only the reply reader was shared (#229). Request building and Basic encoding are also duplicated (:141-158/:184-189 vs :1523-1568).

**Failure scenario.** An authenticating proxy that answers the first CONNECT with `407` plus `Connection: close` (or a chunked body): HTTPS requests through it succeed after the HTTP transport reconnects with credentials, WebSocket connections through the same proxy always fail with ProxyTunnelFailed.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 9.3.6, 11.7.1

## Suggested fix
Move the tunnel loop into one internal helper in TurboHTTP.Transport (WebSocket.Transport already has InternalsVisibleTo) parameterised by credentials/consent and a reconnect callback, and use it from both transports; #187 (fold WebSocket.Transport into Transport) is the natural place but does not list this.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] wss:// through a proxy that answers the first CONNECT with 407 plus Connection: close succeeds after reconnecting with credentials, as HTTPS through RawSocketTransport does
- [ ] One internal CONNECT helper in TurboHTTP.Transport is used by both transports; the duplicated loop is removed
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ against a loopback proxy returning 407 with Connection: close that fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] ProxyCredentials accepts ':' and control characters in the user name, so the Basic header is ambiguous
body:
## Summary
BuildBasicAuthorization joins Username and Password with ':' and Base64-encodes the result, and the ProxyCredentials constructor accepts any string. A user name containing ':' is split at the wrong place by the proxy. This can fail authentication or bind to a different account.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:186`

## Problem
BuildBasicAuthorization concatenates Username + ":" + Password and Base64-encodes the result (ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:184-189); the ProxyCredentials constructor accepts any string (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketProxySettings.cs:9-13).

**Failure scenario.** User name 'corp:alice' with password 'pw' is sent as user 'corp' with password 'alice:pw': authentication fails, or binds to a different account at the proxy.

## Spec reference
RFC 7617 2

## Suggested fix
Reject ':' and control characters in the user-id when the credentials are constructed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ProxyCredentials rejects a user-id containing ':' or control characters with ArgumentException (RFC 7617 section 2)
- [ ] Valid credentials still produce the same Proxy-Authorization header
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ for 'corp:alice' that fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] RawSocketWebSocketTransport leaks the connected socket when ResolveTlsProvider throws
body:
## Summary
EstablishStreamAsync calls ResolveTlsProvider outside the try block that disposes the stream. When the provider is unavailable (wrong provider type or BouncyCastle requested without the opt-in assembly) the exception escapes with the TCP socket still open. Each failed wss:// connect leaves a socket until finalization.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:225`

## Problem
EstablishStreamAsync calls ResolveTlsProvider(options) at :225, outside the try at :227-249 that disposes the stream. ResolveTlsProvider throws ArgumentException for a TlsProvider of the wrong type (:294-296), and TlsProviderSelector.GetProvider throws InvalidOperationException when TlsBackend.BouncyCastle is requested without the opt-in assembly (Runtime/Transport/Tls/TlsProviderSelector.cs:90). ConnectAsync's only catch (:156-160) handles cancellation, so the HoldingNetworkStream created at :142 (TCP connected, possibly with an established CONNECT tunnel) is never disposed.

**Failure scenario.** A wss:// connect with TlsBackend.BouncyCastle in a build without TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE: every ConnectAsync opens a TCP connection, throws, and leaves the socket open until its finalizer runs.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the TLS provider before any socket is opened (it needs only the options), or move the call inside the try.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The TLS provider is resolved before a socket is opened, or inside the try, so the socket is disposed on failure
- [ ] The same exception type is thrown as today
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ asserting the socket is closed after a failed provider resolution, failing before the fix

title: [WebSocket] RawSocketWebSocketTransport ignores its tlsBackend constructor argument because options.TlsBackend is never null
body:
## Summary
ConnectAsync clones the options to a non-null object and resolves the provider with options.TlsBackend ?? _tlsBackend. TlsBackend is a non-nullable enum defaulting to Auto, so the constructor and factory value are never used. A caller requesting BouncyCastle through the constructor silently gets SslStream.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:289`

## Problem
ConnectAsync replaces `options` with a non-null clone (`options = options?.Clone() ?? new WebSocketConnectionOptions();`, :69) and passes it to ResolveTlsProvider, which evaluates `TlsProviderSelector.GetProvider(options?.TlsBackend ?? _tlsBackend)` (:289). `options?.TlsBackend` is never null there, so `_tlsBackend` (set from the public constructor, :25-44) is dead and the provider always follows options.TlsBackend (default Auto). WebSocketTransportFactory.Register takes `Func<TlsBackend, IWebSocketTransport>` (WebSocketTransportFactory.cs:14) and WebSocketClient passes options.TlsBackend into it (WebSocketClient.cs:174, 718-721), i.e. the same value the transport reads from the options anyway. No test constructs the transport with a non-default backend.

**Failure scenario.** `new WebSocketClient(new RawSocketWebSocketTransport(TlsBackend.BouncyCastle))` followed by ConnectAsync(uri) (or any options that leave TlsBackend at Auto) negotiates TLS with the Auto provider (SslStream); the explicitly requested backend is silently ignored.

## Suggested fix
Pick one owner for the backend: either remove the constructor/factory parameter and document options.TlsBackend as the only switch, or make the constructor value the default that an explicitly set option overrides (a nullable option or an 'unset' value).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A TlsBackend passed to the transport constructor or factory is honoured unless options set a non-default backend explicitly, or the parameter is removed and docs name options.TlsBackend as the only switch
- [ ] Behaviour is documented in XML docs
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-10` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ConnectAsync replaces options with a non-null clone (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:69) before EstablishStreamAsync -> ResolveTlsProvider(options), where `options?.TlsBackend ?? _tlsBackend` (:289) can never fall back because TlsBackend is a non-nullable enum property defaulting to Auto (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:113). _tlsBackend, set by the public constructor (:25-44), is therefore never read. The factory path passes options.TlsBackend into the constructor (WebSocketClient.cs:174, 718-721; RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:54-55), i.e. the value the options already carry. A directly constructed RawSocketWebSocketTransport(TlsBackend.BouncyCastle) with default options uses the Auto provider. Not a TLS weakening (both providers validate), but a public constructor argument is silently ignored.

Also reported as `ws-protocol-20` (merged into this issue).

Related: [[R11-ws-runtime-17]].

title: [WebSocket] DNS timeout Task.Delay is never cancelled when the lookup wins, leaving a timer per connect
body:
## Summary
ResolveDnsAsync races the lookup against Task.Delay(timeoutMs, ct) and does not cancel the delay when the lookup completes first. The same pattern is used in ObserveReceiveLoopTerminationAsync. Each connect or reconnect leaves a timer alive for up to 10 s, which accumulates in reconnect storms.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:331`

## Problem
ResolveDnsAsync races the lookup against Task.Delay(timeoutMs, ct) (:331-333) and never cancels the delay when the lookup completes first; the default DnsTimeoutMs is 10 s (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:80). It runs for every connect and again for the NAT64 fallback (:123). ObserveReceiveLoopTerminationAsync does the same with a 1 s delay (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:396).

**Failure scenario.** Each connect or reconnect attempt leaves a timer and its token registration alive for up to 10 s after DNS answered; a reconnect storm accumulates one per attempt.

## Suggested fix
Run the delay on a linked CTS and cancel and dispose it when the lookup completes first.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The delay runs on a linked CancellationTokenSource that is cancelled and disposed when the lookup completes first
- [ ] No timer remains after a successful lookup or receive-loop observation
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix, without wall-clock sleeps

title: [WebSocket] Invalid ws/wss URIs are rejected after the Connecting transition, raising OnError/OnClosed and a retryable NetworkError
body:
## Summary
Public ConnectAsync entry points only check for a null URI before moving to Connecting; scheme and absolute-URI validation happens later in the transport and handshake. A usage error therefore raises events and throws a WebSocketException with a retryable error. Generic retry code keeps retrying a programming error.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:381`

## Problem
WebSocketClient.ConnectAsync and WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync check only for a null URI (WebSocketClient.cs:106-107; WebSocketConnection.cs:156-157) before the None -> Connecting transition (:161). The scheme and absolute-URI checks are in RawSocketWebSocketTransport.ValidateUri (:381-390, ArgumentException) and again in WebSocketHandshake.ValidateUri (WebSocketHandshake.cs:182-197), both inside the connection's try block, whose catch-all converts the ArgumentException to WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed) and runs FinalizeClose (WebSocketConnection.cs:322-365), raising Error/OnError and the Closed transition/OnClosed(1006). With a custom transport the scheme is not checked until the handshake request is built, after the transport has opened a connection.

**Failure scenario.** `await client.ConnectAsync(new Uri("https://example.com/socket"))` raises OnError and OnClosed(AbnormalClosure) and throws a WebSocketException whose HttpError is a retryable NetworkError, so generic retry code keeps retrying a programming error; a relative Uri takes the same path through an InvalidOperationException from Uri.Host.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 3

## Suggested fix
Validate absolute ws/wss URIs once at the public entry points and throw ArgumentException before any state change or event; keep the transport and handshake checks as internal assertions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectAsync throws ArgumentException for non-absolute or non-ws/wss URIs before any state change or event
- [ ] Connection state stays None and no OnError/OnClosed is raised
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ for https:// and relative URIs that fails before the fix

title: [Packaging] TurboHTTP.Complete bootstrap always roots the WebSocket transport, so HTTP-only builds link it
body:
## Summary
The Complete bootstrap calls RawSocketWebSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered() unconditionally and the WebSocket.Transport link.xml preserves the transport with preserve="all". An HTTP-only project using Complete still links the WebSocket connect path and proxy tunnel. Folding the transport into Transport (#187) would not remove this root.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/link.xml:10`

## Problem
TurboHTTP.Complete is [AlwaysLinkAssembly] and its [Preserve] bootstrap calls RawSocketWebSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered() unconditionally (Runtime/Bootstrap/TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:54), and Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/link.xml preserves RawSocketWebSocketTransport and WebSocketTransportModuleInitializer with preserve="all" (:9-10; merged by Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor whenever the assembly is in the build). That roots RawSocketWebSocketTransport (403 lines), ProxyTunnelConnector (191) and, through their signatures and bodies, WebSocketConnectionOptions.Clone/Validate (342), WebSocketProxySettings (141), WebSocketReconnectPolicy (136), WebSocketException (140), WebSocketTransportFactory and the enums: roughly 1,000 to 1,400 source lines of WebSocket code in a build that never opens a socket. There is no define or setting to skip the registration; the only opt-out is excluding Complete and re-doing the HTTP transport and JSON registration by hand. Runtime/WebSocket/link.xml additionally preserves SHA1, SHA1Managed (not instantiated by this module, which calls SHA1.Create()) and RandomNumberGenerator with preserve="all" in mscorlib whenever the assembly is present. #187's acceptance criterion 'HTTP-only builds do not pull WebSocket code' covers the goal, but its proposed fix (move the sources into TurboHTTP.Transport) keeps the bootstrap call and the preserve rule, so the code would then be rooted inside the always-needed transport assembly.

**Failure scenario.** A size-sensitive mobile title uses only UHttpClient with the default Complete setup: the IL2CPP build carries the WebSocket connect path, proxy tunnel, options validation and exception mapping (plus whatever Unity.WebSocket MonoBehaviours UnityLinker keeps) with no supported way to drop them short of dismantling the bootstrap.

## Suggested fix
Register the WebSocket default lazily from code that only WebSocket users reach (for example WebSocketTransportFactory resolving a default supplied by a tiny registration stub, or the bootstrap gated by a define/scripting symbol), drop the preserve="all" rule once nothing needs reflection, and record in #187 that the registration root must move with the fold.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The WebSocket default registration is reachable only from WebSocket code or gated by a define, not from the unconditional bootstrap
- [ ] The preserve="all" link.xml rule is removed or narrowed
- [ ] An HTTP-only IL2CPP build no longer links RawSocketWebSocketTransport, recorded with a build-size comparison
- [ ] #187 notes that the registration root must move with the fold

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-23` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The root is real and statically traceable; the size it costs depends on UnityLinker and is small. TurboHTTP.Complete is [AlwaysLinkAssembly] (Runtime/Bootstrap/AssemblyInfo.cs:8), its [Preserve] bootstrap calls RawSocketWebSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered() unconditionally with no define (Runtime/Bootstrap/TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:45-54), and Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/link.xml preserves RawSocketWebSocketTransport and WebSocketTransportModuleInitializer with preserve="all" (:9-10), merged whenever the assembly is in the build (Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:20-22, :147-149). ConnectAsync then keeps ProxyTunnelConnector, WebSocketConnectionOptions.Clone/Validate, WebSocketProxySettings, WebSocketException and WebSocketTransportFactory reachable (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:58-176). Complete also references TurboHTTP.Unity.WebSocket (Runtime/TurboHTTP.Complete.asmdef); what UnityLinker keeps of its MonoBehaviours cannot be settled statically. Runtime/WebSocket/link.xml preserves SHA1, SHA1Managed and RandomNumberGenerator while the module only calls SHA1.Create() (WebSocketConstants.cs:58, :198), a negligible cost. #187 tracks the goal through its acceptance criterion 'HTTP-only builds do not pull WebSocket code'; the finding's addition is correct and worth recording there: moving the sources into TurboHTTP.Transport as #187 proposes leaves the bootstrap call and the preserve rule, so the criterion is not met by the fold alone. Severity low: on the order of 1,000-1,400 source lines retained, with a documented manual opt-out (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:26-29).

title: [WebSocket] IWebSocketExtension has no documented contract or negotiated-limit context, and Reset() is never called
body:
## Summary
IWebSocketExtension has no XML docs on any member, Reset() is never invoked by the connection, and TransformOutbound and TransformInbound run on different threads without that being stated. Implementers also never learn the negotiated size limits before the post-check. Third-party extensions can corrupt shared state or inflate zip-bomb input.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/IWebSocketExtension.cs:11`

## Problem
The interface has no XML documentation on any member (IWebSocketExtension.cs:11-26). `Reset()` (:25) is never invoked: the only `.Reset()` call in the module is on the message assembler (Lifecycle.cs:188). TransformOutbound runs on the sender's thread under the message lock (Extensions.cs:24-54) while TransformInbound runs on the receive loop (:90-108), i.e. concurrently on one instance, which is not stated. The ownership of the returned IMemoryOwner and the meaning of a null return are implicit. An implementation is not told MaxMessageSize, so a decompressing extension can only bound its output by capturing a value at factory-creation time (see ws-design-12); the connection checks the size after the transform (Extensions.cs:132). The zero-copy hand-off works only for Core's internal ArrayPoolMemoryOwner<byte> (Extensions.cs:142-147); any other owner is copied. Compression metrics are attributed by a hard-coded name test (`"permessage-deflate"`, Extensions.cs:274). PerMessageDeflateExtension.Reset is an empty method (PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:239-243).

**Failure scenario.** A third-party compression extension keeps per-direction state in shared fields (as the single-instance interface suggests) and corrupts it when a send and a receive overlap; or it inflates a 4 MB limit's worth of zip-bomb input to gigabytes because it never learns the limit before the connection's post-check.

## Spec reference
RFC 7692 7.2

## Suggested fix
Document threading, ownership and null semantics; remove Reset or call it at defined points; pass a context with the negotiated limits to the factory or to TransformInbound; accept any IMemoryOwner without an internal-type fast path being the only cheap route (#76 tracks the wider InternalsVisibleTo gap).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] XML docs describe threading, buffer ownership and null semantics for every member
- [ ] Reset is either removed or called at defined points
- [ ] Extensions receive the negotiated message limit so inflation is bounded before the connection post-check
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ for the limit being enforced, failing before the fix

title: [WebSocket] MessageAssembler holds one pooled buffer per fragment and copies them into a second buffer, with a low fragment cap
body:
## Summary
TryStageFragment keeps each fragment's pooled buffer and AssembleFragmentedMessageAndReset rents a second buffer and copies all fragments into it. Peak memory is about double, and a fragment-count cap of 64 rejects finely fragmented messages with 1009 even far below MaxMessageSize.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/MessageAssembler.cs:218`

## Problem
TryStageFragment detaches each fragment's pooled buffer into _fragments (:191-204); AssembleFragmentedMessageAndReset then rents a second buffer of the total size and copies every fragment (:218-229) before the fragments are returned (:234). Rent rounds each buffer up to a power of two, so the message is held twice (up to about 4x MaxMessageSize of pooled memory at the peak) and copied once more than a single growing buffer would need. The per-fragment array and lease are why MaxFragmentCount (default 64, WebSocketConstants.cs:26) caps the fragment count independently of the byte limit (:155-164).

**Failure scenario.** A 4 MB message sent in 64 KB fragments holds 64 pooled 64 KB arrays plus a 4 MB array at completion and is copied in full; a message fragmented more finely than 64 frames (servers that fragment at 4-8 KB) is rejected with 1009 although it is far below MaxMessageSize.

## Suggested fix
Append fragments into one pooled growable buffer bounded by MaxMessageSize (read later fragments directly into it), which removes the final copy and lets the fragment cap become a derived, much larger bound.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fragments are appended into one pooled growable buffer bounded by MaxMessageSize with no final copy
- [ ] A 4 MB message in 4 KB fragments is accepted
- [ ] Peak pooled bytes for a fragmented message stay at or below 2x message size, measured in a test
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] permessage-deflate allocates a DeflateStream and MemoryStreams per message and copies the body three to four times
body:
## Summary
PerMessageDeflateExtension creates a new DeflateStream, payload-sized MemoryStreams and extra copies for every message in both directions. On Unity's non-generational GC this produces large short-lived garbage. Compressed feeds of large JSON messages are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:252`

## Problem
Outbound: Compress (:250-316) allocates a MemoryStream with a payload-sized array (:252) and a new DeflateStream with its native deflate state per message (:255-258), then copies the result into a pooled owner (:309-311). Inbound: Decompress (:318-395) copies the whole compressed payload into a pooled array to append 00 00 FF FF (:333-340), creates two MemoryStreams and a DeflateStream (:342-344), inflates through a 16 KB chunk into a doubling MemoryStream (:349-361) and copies that into a pooled owner (:378-386). Reset() (:239-243) confirms that nothing is kept between messages.

**Failure scenario.** A feed of 100 KB compressed JSON messages allocates per message about 100 KB (outbound) or about 260 KB of doubling MemoryStream arrays (inbound) of managed garbage plus a DeflateStream and its native zlib state. On Unity's non-generational Boehm GC these large short-lived arrays fragment and grow the heap; with the 128-byte CompressionThreshold even a 200-byte message pays a full deflate-state setup.

## Suggested fix
Inflate and deflate into a pooled growable writer instead of MemoryStream (detach it as the owner, no final copy), feed the tail through a two-segment read stream instead of copying the payload, and keep one inflater/deflater per connection where the negotiated parameters allow it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Compress and decompress use pooled growable writers with no final copy and no payload copy to append the 00 00 FF FF tail
- [ ] Managed allocation per 100 KB message is reduced to a stated target below the current figures, measured in a test
- [ ] Context takeover reuses one inflater/deflater per connection where negotiated
- [ ] Regression/allocation test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-12` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced in PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs. Inbound always: payload copied into a pooled array to append the tail (:333-340), two MemoryStreams + a new DeflateStream (:342-344), growth through a non-pooled MemoryStream (:361), final copy into a pooled owner (:378-386). Outbound Compress: MemoryStream(payload.Length + 32) (:252), new DeflateStream (:255-258), copy to owner (:309-311); Reset() keeps nothing (:239-243). One nuance the finding omits: on runtimes whose Flush does not sync-flush (Unity Mono/IL2CPP) and when client_no_context_takeover is NOT agreed, outbound goes through the pooled managed SyncFlushDeflater (:163-174) instead. The default option offers client_no_context_takeover (PerMessageDeflateOptions.cs:31), so when the server agrees the DeflateStream path is the per-message path as described. Compression is opt-in. #104 covers permessage-deflate verification gates, not this cost.

title: [WebSocket] server_max_window_bits is parsed with culture-sensitive lenient int.TryParse
body:
## Summary
TryParseWindowBits uses int.TryParse with the current culture and default styles. A value such as "+015" or one with surrounding whitespace is accepted although RFC 7692 defines a decimal integer without leading zeros. The client must fail the negotiation on an invalid value.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:421`

## Problem
TryParseWindowBits calls int.TryParse(value, out bits) (PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:415-425): current culture and NumberStyles.Integer, so surrounding whitespace (possible in a quoted value, IWebSocketExtension.cs:264-295), a leading '+' and leading zeros are accepted.

**Failure scenario.** A response 'permessage-deflate; server_no_context_takeover; server_max_window_bits="+015"' is accepted as 15, although the value is defined as a decimal integer without leading zeros between 8 and 15 and the client must fail the connection on an invalid value.

## Spec reference
RFC 7692 7.1.2.1

## Suggested fix
Parse one or two ASCII digits by hand (no leading zero), or use NumberStyles.None with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture and reject a leading '0'.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Only 8 to 15 written as plain ASCII digits without a leading zero or sign is accepted
- [ ] Invalid values fail the connection per RFC 7692 section 7.1.2.1
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ for "+015", " 15" and "08" that fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient stacks three bounded receive queues and three pump tasks per socket
body:
## Summary
WebSocketConnection, WebSocketClient and ResilientWebSocketClient each own a receive queue with the full configured budget and pump into the next. A stalled consumer can hold three times ReceiveQueueMaxBytes before backpressure reaches TCP, and every message pays extra hops. This matters on memory-constrained mobile targets.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:115`

## Problem
WebSocketConnection owns `_receiveQueue` (WebSocketConnection.cs:174), WebSocketClient pumps it into its own `_messageQueue` through RunReceiveListenerAsync (WebSocketClient.cs:153, 396-460), and ResilientWebSocketClient wraps a WebSocketClient and pumps that into `_incomingQueue` through RunReceivePumpAsync (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:115, 340-342, 386-452). All three are created by WebSocketMessageQueue.Create(options) with the same ReceiveQueueCapacity and ReceiveQueueMaxBytes. The option documents two queues ('the connection queue and the client queue', WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:35-42). Even a plain pull consumer of WebSocketClient goes through a second queue and task hop although ReceiveAsync could read the connection queue directly when no OnMessage handler is subscribed.

**Failure scenario.** A pull consumer of a ResilientWebSocketClient that stalls lets up to 3 x ReceiveQueueMaxBytes (24 MB by default, plus one in-flight message per pump) and 3 x ReceiveQueueCapacity messages accumulate before TCP backpressure starts, three times what the option promises on a memory-constrained mobile target; every message pays two extra lock/await hops.

## Suggested fix
Let the resilient client own WebSocketConnection instances directly (or give WebSocketClient an internal pass-through receive path) so there is one delivery queue per client; at minimum document and divide the byte budget across layers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One delivery queue per client, or the byte budget is divided across layers so total buffered bytes do not exceed ReceiveQueueMaxBytes
- [ ] Extra pump tasks and lock hops are removed or documented
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ asserting total buffered bytes with a stalled consumer, failing before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-13` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Three queues are created with the same budgets through WebSocketMessageQueue.Create(options) (AsyncBoundedQueue.cs:287-293): WebSocketConnection._receiveQueue (WebSocketConnection.cs:174), WebSocketClient._messageQueue (WebSocketClient.cs:153) fed by RunReceiveListenerAsync (:396-460), and ResilientWebSocketClient._incomingQueue (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:115) fed by RunReceivePumpAsync (:386-452) from an inner WebSocketClient (:340-342). The inner client has no OnMessage subscriber (only metrics/quality handlers are attached, :343-344), so its listener uses the lossless EnqueueAsync path (WebSocketClient.cs:410-423); a stalled puller therefore fills all three queues, each pump holding one more message, before the connection read loop parks (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:299-300). Defaults: 100 messages / 8 MB per queue (WebSocketConstants.cs:28-31), so about 24 MB plus up to three in-flight messages of MaxMessageSize for the resilient client and 16 MB for the plain client. The option doc says 'each' queue and names two (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:35-42), but the user documentation promises one budget: 'queued losslessly, up to ReceiveQueueCapacity messages (default 100) and ReceiveQueueMaxBytes payload bytes (default 8 MB). When either budget is reached, reading from the socket pauses' (Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:107-112). Memory stays bounded (no DoS), so the defect is a 2x-3x overshoot of the documented bound plus two extra queue/task hops per message. No open issue tracks it.

Also reported as `ws-runtime-14` (merged into this issue).

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient.ConnectAsync resets state while the previous pump or reconnect loop is still running
body:
## Summary
ConnectAsync replaces the incoming queue, disposes the previous lifecycle CancellationTokenSource without cancelling it and resets the manual-close flag without waiting for the previous pump or reconnect loop. An aborted pump can then treat the abort as an unexpected disconnect and run the reconnect loop against the new connection. Applications that call Abort() followed by ConnectAsync() are affected, depending on thread-pool scheduling.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:116`

## Problem
ConnectAsync (:105-123) replaces _incomingQueue, disposes the previous _lifecycleCts without cancelling it (:116) and resets _manualClose (:119), with no check of _reconnectLoopActive and before the previous pump has ended (it is awaited only later, :338). Abort() (:252-268) does not wait for the pump. A pump whose token was disposed but not cancelled passes the '!ct.IsCancellationRequested' test (:450) and enters the reconnect loop, which reads the already reset _manualClose (:552). TryEnterReconnectLoop rejects a stale client only when a loop is already active (:512-521); with no loop active, a disconnect of a client that is no longer _client takes the loop, which then disposes whatever _client is current (:576-582) or completes the new queue (:610).

**Failure scenario.** 'client.Abort(); await client.ConnectAsync(uri, options);' (a reconnect-now action): ConnectAsync resets _manualClose before the aborted pump's continuation runs on the pool. That pump treats the abort as an unexpected disconnect: OnError, OnReconnecting, a backoff delay that ConnectAsync waits behind (:338), a second connection that ConnectAsync immediately replaces; the replaced client's pump then takes the loop and tears down the user's new connection or, when its close code is not reconnectable, completes the new receive queue while the connection is Open. The same happens when ConnectAsync is called while a reconnect loop is active (State reports Connecting but :107 allows it). Depends on thread-pool scheduling; a test that aborts and reconnects immediately with a subscribed OnReconnecting would confirm it.

## Suggested fix
In ConnectAsync cancel (not only dispose) the previous lifecycle CTS and wait for the previous pump and loop before resetting _manualClose and the queue; reject ConnectAsync while _reconnectLoopActive; make TryEnterReconnectLoop ignore a client that is not the current _client in every case.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectAsync cancels the previous lifecycle token and awaits the previous pump and reconnect loop before resetting _manualClose or the queue.
- [ ] ConnectAsync throws InvalidOperationException while a reconnect loop is active.
- [ ] A disconnect of a child client that is no longer the current _client never tears down the current connection or completes the new queue.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ calls Abort() then ConnectAsync() immediately with a subscribed OnReconnecting and asserts no reconnect and no teardown of the new connection and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described. ConnectAsync replaces the queue, disposes the old lifecycle CTS without cancelling it and resets _manualClose (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:115-119) before the previous pump is awaited (:338); Abort does not wait for the pump (:252-268); :107 allows ConnectAsync while a reconnect loop is in backoff (the dead child is Closed). TryEnterReconnectLoop rejects a stale client only when a loop is already active (:512-521). Trace for 'Abort(); ConnectAsync()' with the default policy None: the aborted pump's continuation is queued to the pool (queue waiters park on SemaphoreSlim.WaitAsync, AsyncBoundedQueue.cs:186, :208-209), ConnectAsync's lock block runs first, the old pump then sees a non-cancelled token (:450) and _manualClose == 0 (:552), raises OnError and calls CompleteAndDrainQueue on the new queue (:610) and a second OnClosed, so the new connection's ReceiveAsync fails at once while the child stays Open. With a policy enabled the stale loop reconnects and the replaced child's pump later takes the loop and disposes the user's connection (:576-581). Not settled statically: the first step is a thread-pool race (an OnClosed handler that runs long enough lets the old pump read _manualClose == 1 first), and on Unity Mono registering on the disposed CTS token (Task.Delay at :574, CreateLinkedTokenSource at :335) may throw ObjectDisposedException, which changes the enabled-policy outcome to a stray OnError. No test covers Abort-then-Connect on the resilient client (WebSocketClientReconnectTests.AbortThenConnect covers WebSocketClient only).

Related: [[R11-ws-protocol-01]], [[R11-ws-runtime-04]].

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketClient and ResilientWebSocketClient duplicate receive plumbing and the copies have diverged
body:
## Summary
The two clients each implement the receive front end (exclusivity flags, queue, enumerable, OnMessage dispatch, closed-exception construction) and the copies differ. ReceiveAsync before ConnectAsync throws NullReferenceException on the resilient client, and a pull consumer of the resilient client loses the server close code that the plain client reports. Application-level close handling therefore behaves differently per client type.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:212`

## Problem
ReceiveAllAsync (WebSocketClient.cs:242-268 vs ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:174-198), ReceiveCoreAsync (270-311 vs 200-225), the pump loop with its five catch clauses (396-460 vs 386-452), RaiseMessage (492-508 vs 454-467) and CompleteAndDrainQueue (683-690 vs 694-702) are copies, sharing only PublishDroppingOldest. Differences: WebSocketClient.ReceiveCoreAsync checks the state and throws InvalidOperationException for None, the resilient copy has no state check and dereferences `_incomingQueue`, which is null until the first ConnectAsync (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:212); WebSocketClient attaches the close code and reason to the ConnectionClosed exception (WebSocketClient.cs:297-305), the resilient copy drops them (:216-219) although the terminal error is available as the queue's completion error; only the resilient SendAsync maps ObjectDisposedException (:140-143).

**Failure scenario.** `new ResilientWebSocketClient().ReceiveAsync()` before ConnectAsync throws NullReferenceException instead of InvalidOperationException; after a server close with code 4001 a pull consumer of the resilient client gets a WebSocketException with CloseCode null where the plain client reports 4001, so application-level close handling works with one client type and not the other.

## Suggested fix
Factor the shared receive front end (exclusivity flags, queue, enumerable, OnMessage dispatch, closed-exception construction) into one internal helper used by both clients, or build the resilient client on WebSocketConnection directly (see ws-design-13).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The shared receive front end lives in one internal helper used by both clients.
- [ ] ReceiveAsync before ConnectAsync throws InvalidOperationException on both clients.
- [ ] After a server close with code 4001 the pull consumer of both clients gets a WebSocketException with CloseCode 4001.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ runs the same receive-before-connect and close-code cases against both clients and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-22` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Both divergences traced. (1) ResilientWebSocketClient.ReceiveCoreAsync has no state check and awaits `_incomingQueue.DequeueAsync` (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:200-212); _incomingQueue is assigned only in ConnectAsync (:115), so ReceiveAsync on a never-connected instance throws NullReferenceException, where WebSocketClient throws InvalidOperationException (WebSocketClient.cs:276-283). ReceiveAllAsync is guarded (State == None check, ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:178-183); only ReceiveAsync is affected. (2) Close code: on a server close 4001 the inner client reports WebSocketException with CloseCode 4001 (WebSocketClient.cs:295-305), the pump takes it as terminalError (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:434-437), the default policy does not reconnect on 4001 (WebSocketReconnectPolicy.cs:123-134), and RunReconnectLoopAsync completes the queue with that error and raises OnClosed(4001) (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:610-613). The puller then gets AsyncQueueCompletedException(inner = terminalError) (AsyncBoundedQueue.cs:178-179) and the resilient copy wraps it without code or reason (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:214-219), so CloseCode is null and the real code is only at InnerException.InnerException. The duplicated blocks are as listed (ReceiveAllAsync, ReceiveCoreAsync, pump loop, RaiseMessage, CompleteAndDrainQueue), sharing only PublishDroppingOldest (WebSocketClient.cs:466). No test covers either case (rg over Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/*Resilient* and WebSocketClientReconnectTests). Both are edge cases (misuse before connect; pull consumers reading the code from the exception instead of OnClosed).

Related: [[R11-ws-protocol-02]], [[R11-ws-design-20]].

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient.CloseAsync detaches the child client before the close can fail, orphaning a live connection
body:
## Summary
CloseAsync sets the child client to null before calling the child's CloseAsync. If the child's CloseAsync throws, for example on an invalid close code, the connection stays open and its pump keeps delivering messages while the wrapper reports State None. Dispose then no longer disposes the child, so its socket and keep-alive loop leak.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:237`

## Problem
`var client = Interlocked.Exchange(ref _client, null)` (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:237) precedes `await client.CloseAsync(code, reason, ct)` (242), and DisposeAsync (243) is not in a finally. WebSocketConnection.CloseAsync throws InvalidCloseCode for 1005/1006/1015 without touching the connection (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:102-107), and ArgumentException in the case of ws-protocol-16.

**Failure scenario.** `resilient.CloseAsync(WebSocketCloseCode.AbnormalClosure)` throws. The child stays Open and its pump keeps delivering messages, but _client is null: State is None, SendAsync throws, a second CloseAsync awaits the live pump in StopReceivePumpAsync until the server closes, and Dispose no longer disposes the child, so its socket and keep-alive loop leak.

## Suggested fix
Validate the code before detaching, and dispose or abort the child in a finally (or restore _client when CloseAsync throws).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CloseAsync validates the close code before detaching the child.
- [ ] If the child's CloseAsync throws, the child is aborted or disposed, or _client is restored; no live connection is left without an owner.
- [ ] A second CloseAsync does not block on a live pump after a failed first close.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ passes AbnormalClosure to CloseAsync and asserts the child is disposed or still owned and no socket leaks and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-protocol-17` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient publishes a freshly connected child without re-checking disposal
body:
## Summary
After a connect completes, the client assigns the new child to _client without checking whether Dispose or a manual close ran meanwhile. A Dispose racing the end of a connect leaves a live connection that is never disposed, and OnReconnected or OnConnected can fire after OnClosed. This affects reconnect attempts and the initial ConnectAsync.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:361`

## Problem
ConnectReplacementClientAsync awaits nextClient.ConnectAsync (:351) and then unconditionally does Interlocked.Exchange(ref _client, nextClient) (:361), stores the latest metrics and starts a pump (:369-372). Dispose()/DisposeAsync() take _client once (:279, :304) and never look again; nothing after :351 re-reads _disposed or the lifecycle token. The same method reads _lifecycleCts without synchronisation (:334-335) although Dispose disposes and nulls it (:291-292, :325-326).

**Failure scenario.** Dispose lands between the last cancellation check inside the child's connect (WebSocketConnection.cs:263) and :361, during a reconnect attempt or the initial ConnectAsync. Dispose has already exchanged _client, so the new child becomes _client after disposal: its pump exits at once (token cancelled), OnReconnected/OnConnected fires after OnClosed, and the child connection (socket, receive loop, keep-alive pings) is never closed. If Dispose wins slightly earlier, :335 throws NullReferenceException or ObjectDisposedException, which the loop reports through OnError after disposal (:597-601).

## Suggested fix
After the connect, publish under _sync only if neither _disposed nor _manualClose is set and the lifecycle token is not cancelled; otherwise dispose nextClient. Capture the lifecycle CTS and token under the same lock.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The new child is published under _sync only if _disposed and _manualClose are unset and the lifecycle token is not cancelled; otherwise it is disposed.
- [ ] OnConnected and OnReconnected never fire after OnClosed.
- [ ] The lifecycle CTS and token are captured under the same lock.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ disposes the client between the child's final cancellation check and publication and asserts the child is disposed and no event fires after OnClosed and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: after 'await nextClient.ConnectAsync' (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:351) nothing re-reads _disposed or the lifecycle token before Interlocked.Exchange(ref _client, nextClient) (:361), and Dispose/DisposeAsync take _client only once (:279, :304). _lifecycleCts is read unsynchronised at :334-335 while Dispose disposes and nulls it (:291-292). Severity lowered: the lifecycle token is linked into the child's connect (:335, :351), so a Dispose at any earlier point cancels it (stream disposed by the handshake registration, WebSocketConnection.cs:200, or the check at :263). The leaking window is only the synchronous stretch from WebSocketConnection.cs:263 to ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:361 (microseconds), and the :335 NRE/ObjectDisposed window is similarly narrow and ends in a stray OnError. Real but rare; the missing re-check is the same gap that makes ws-protocol-01 deterministic for CloseAsync/Abort.

Related: [[R11-ws-runtime-05]], [[R11-ws-protocol-01]].

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient reconnect loop invokes OnError, OnReconnecting and OnReconnected unguarded in an unobserved task
body:
## Summary
The reconnect loop calls user event handlers directly. A throwing OnError or OnReconnecting handler faults the pump task unobserved, leaves a dead child in _client, never completes the queue and never raises OnClosed, so ReceiveAsync hangs and no reconnect happens. A throwing OnReconnected handler is caught as a connect failure and the loop tears down each new connection.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:561`

## Problem
RunReconnectLoopAsync raises OnError (:561, :601), OnReconnecting (:571-572) and, through ConnectReplacementClientAsync, OnReconnected (:381-382) with no try/catch; only OnMessage is guarded (:454-467). The loop runs inside the pump task, which nothing observes (sync Dispose never awaits it; StopReceivePumpAsync swallows). ReleaseDisconnectedClientAsync skips disposal while the dead client is still _client (:618-619).

**Failure scenario.** An OnError or OnReconnecting handler throws: the exception leaves RunReconnectLoopAsync before the delay, the loop flag is cleared, the pump task faults unobserved, the dead child stays in _client, the queue is never completed and OnClosed never fires, so ReceiveAsync hangs and no reconnect is attempted. An OnReconnected handler throws: the exception is caught at :597 as a failed connect, the healthy new connection is disposed at :576-581 on the next iteration, and the client reconnects and tears down again until the policy is exhausted.

## Suggested fix
Invoke user events through one guarded helper, and treat only exceptions from the connect itself as connect failures (raise OnReconnected outside that try). Complete the queue and raise OnClosed if the loop ends by an unexpected exception.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] User events are invoked through one guarded helper that swallows and reports handler exceptions without affecting the loop.
- [ ] Only exceptions from the connect itself count as connect failures; OnReconnected is raised outside that try.
- [ ] If the loop ends by an unexpected exception the queue is completed and OnClosed is raised.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ registers throwing OnError, OnReconnecting and OnReconnected handlers and asserts reconnection continues and ReceiveAsync completes and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RaiseError (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:561, :601, :704-708), OnReconnecting (:571-572) and OnConnected/OnReconnected (:376-382) are invoked with no try/catch; only OnMessage is guarded (:454-467). A throw at :561 or :572 leaves RunReconnectLoopAsync before any reconnect: the finally at :486-490 clears the loop flag, ReleaseDisconnectedClientAsync returns early because the dead child is still _client (:618-619), the queue is never completed and OnClosed never fires; the pump task faults unobserved (sync Dispose never awaits it, StopReceivePumpAsync swallows at :688-691), so ReceiveAsync hangs and no reconnect happens. A throw from OnReconnected happens inside the try at :584-589 after the child was published, is caught at :597 as a connect failure, and the next iteration disposes the healthy connection (:576-581) and reconnects, repeating until the policy is exhausted. Same exposure limit as ws-runtime-01: UnityWebSocketBridge dispatches user handlers guarded, so this needs a throwing handler subscribed directly on ResilientWebSocketClient. No test uses a throwing handler.

Related: [[R11-ws-protocol-01]].

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient keeps reconnecting after CloseAsync or Abort during backoff and leaves a live connection after OnClosed
body:
## Summary
When CloseAsync or Abort is called while the client is in reconnect backoff, the loop is not cancelled and does not re-check the manual-close flag after the delay or after a successful connect. It reconnects with the stored URI and custom headers (including authorization), raises OnReconnected, and the connection stays open until Dispose. CloseAsync can also block for the whole retry budget. Applications that close on logout are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:568`

## Problem
_manualClose is read once, at the top of RunReconnectLoopAsync (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:552). The loop `while (!ct.IsCancellationRequested && policy.ShouldReconnect(...))` (568) awaits Task.Delay(delay, ct) (574) and then calls ConnectReplacementClientAsync (586) without re-checking it. ct is the lifecycle token, which only Dispose/DisposeAsync cancel (277, 302); CloseAsync (227-250) and Abort (252-268) set _manualClose and null _client but do not cancel it. CloseAsync then awaits the pump task that is running this very loop (StopReceivePumpAsync 676-692; the pump ends in HandleUnexpectedDisconnectAsync, 451). On a successful reconnect _client = nextClient (361), a new pump starts (372), OnReconnected fires (381), and ReleaseDisconnectedClientAsync returns early for the current client (618). Tests cover only DisposeDuringBackoff_CancelsReconnectLoop (Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketReconnectionTests.cs:84).

**Failure scenario.** The network drops and the client is in backoff. The app calls Abort() or CloseAsync() (for example on logout) and receives OnClosed. When the server is reachable again the loop connects with the stored URI and CustomHeaders (auth), raises OnReconnected, State is Open, SendAsync works and OnMessage keeps firing; the connection lives until Dispose. With WebSocketReconnectPolicy.Infinite and an unreachable server CloseAsync never returns; with Default it blocks through all retries (delays plus a 10 s handshake timeout each).

## Suggested fix
Cancel a per-connect CancellationTokenSource from CloseAsync and Abort, and re-check _manualClose/_disposed after the delay and after a successful connect (dispose the replacement instead of publishing it). Add tests for CloseAsync and Abort during backoff.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CloseAsync and Abort cancel the in-flight backoff delay and connect through a per-connect CancellationTokenSource.
- [ ] _manualClose and _disposed are re-checked after the delay and after a successful connect; a replacement connection is disposed instead of published.
- [ ] CloseAsync returns without waiting for the retry budget.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ calls CloseAsync and Abort during backoff and asserts no reconnect, no OnReconnected and State stays closed and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-protocol-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RunReconnectLoopAsync reads _manualClose only at entry (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:552); the loop condition (:568) and the code after Task.Delay (:574-591) test only ct, the lifecycle token, which only Dispose/DisposeAsync cancel (:277, :302). Abort (:252-268) and CloseAsync (:227-250) set _manualClose and null _client but cancel nothing. After the delay the loop calls ConnectReplacementClientAsync, which publishes the new child unconditionally (:361), starts a pump (:372) and raises OnReconnected (:381-382) after OnClosed was already raised. CloseAsync additionally awaits the pump task that is running this loop (StopReceivePumpAsync :676-692, no ct), so it blocks for the remaining attempts and never returns with WebSocketReconnectPolicy.Infinite (WebSocketReconnectPolicy.cs:17) and an unreachable server. UnityWebSocketClient.CloseConnectionAsync (Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketClient.cs:499-502) goes through this CloseAsync. No guard found; the only backoff test is DisposeDuringBackoff_CancelsReconnectLoop (Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketReconnectionTests.cs:84). One detail of the scenario is wrong: OnMessage does not keep firing. The queue was completed by Abort/CloseAsync, so the first inbound message throws AsyncQueueCompletedException in the new pump (AsyncBoundedQueue.cs:92, :152), the loop is re-entered, sees _manualClose (:552) and returns, and ReleaseDisconnectedClientAsync skips disposal because the client is still _client (:618). The child stays Open (socket, pings, SendAsync works, State == Open, later ConnectAsync throws at :107) until Dispose.

Also reported as `ws-design-02`, `ws-runtime-02` (merged into this issue).

Related: [[R11-ws-runtime-05]], [[R11-ws-runtime-04]], [[R11-ws-runtime-06]].

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient discards messages queued for ReceiveAsync when the connection ends terminally
body:
## Summary
On a server Close with a non-reconnect code, or when retries are exhausted, the client drains the incoming queue instead of completing it. A consumer that has read only part of the delivered messages loses the rest and gets ConnectionClosed early. The plain WebSocketClient completes the queue without draining it, so the two clients behave differently.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:610`

## Problem
In pull-only mode the pump moves every message into _incomingQueue (405). When the child reports the close, RunReconnectLoopAsync ends with CompleteAndDrainQueue(terminalError) (610; also 554), which calls queue.Complete and then queue.Drain(dispose) (694-702). BoundedAsyncQueue.DequeueAsync would still hand out queued items after Complete (AsyncBoundedQueue.cs:175-179), which is how WebSocketClient keeps messages that arrived ahead of the peer's Close (#217: WebSocketClient.cs:456-459 completes without draining; Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketReceiveAfterCloseTests.cs). The resilient wrapper's Drain throws them away. No resilient-client test covers messages ahead of a close.

**Failure scenario.** A server sends five result messages and then Close(1000). The inner client delivers all five to the pump, which enqueues them and then sees ConnectionClosed with code 1000; ShouldReconnect is false, so the queue is drained. An app pulling with ReceiveAllAsync that has consumed only the first message (one message per Unity frame) gets ConnectionClosed next: messages 2-5 are lost without any error. The same happens when retries are exhausted after an abnormal drop.

## Suggested fix
On connection-end paths complete _incomingQueue without draining it (drain only in Dispose and on an explicit CloseAsync/Abort), as WebSocketClient does, and add a regression test equivalent to WebSocketReceiveAfterCloseTests for ResilientWebSocketClient.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On terminal connection end the queue is completed without draining; queued messages are still delivered before the closed exception.
- [ ] Draining happens only in Dispose and on an explicit CloseAsync or Abort.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ mirrors WebSocketReceiveAfterCloseTests for ResilientWebSocketClient: five messages then Close(1000), consumer reads all five and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-protocol-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Pull-only pump moves each message into _incomingQueue (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:405). When the child reports the close, RunReconnectLoopAsync falls through to CompleteAndDrainQueue(terminalError) (:610), which does queue.Complete then queue.Drain(dispose) (:700-701). BoundedAsyncQueue.DequeueAsync would return queued items before reporting completion (AsyncBoundedQueue.cs:175-179), so it is the Drain that discards them. For Close(1000) DefaultReconnectOnCloseCode returns false (WebSocketReconnectPolicy.cs:129-134) and with policy None Enabled is false, so the terminal path is taken on every normal close. WebSocketClient deliberately does not drain on this path (#217: WebSocketClient.cs:456-459, :523-526) and Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:94-97 and :108 promise that messages ahead of the close stay readable and that pull-only delivery is lossless, for both clients. No resilient-client test covers messages ahead of a close (WebSocketReceiveAfterCloseTests uses WebSocketClient only). Loss needs the consumer to lag the pump at the moment the close is processed (frame-paced or slow consumer); a consumer already parked in ReceiveAsync normally wins because the close is finalized only after the server closes TCP.

Related: [[R11-ws-design-22]].

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient reconnect loop treats 3xx handshake rejections as transient
body:
## Summary
A handshake answered with a 3xx status is retried like a network failure. Redirects are not followed, so the client re-requests the old URL until the retry budget ends, or forever with WebSocketReconnectPolicy.Infinite, and never raises OnClosed. The application never learns the status or Location.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:651`

## Problem
IsPermanentConnectFailure returns true only for 4xx other than 408/429 and for the proxy 407 (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:639-652). Redirects are never followed: the validator fails every status other than 101 (WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:178-196), so a 301/302/307/308 answer repeats on every attempt. The test rows for IsPermanentConnectFailure are in Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshakeRejectTests.cs:162.

**Failure scenario.** An endpoint moves and answers 301 with Location. A client on WebSocketReconnectPolicy.Infinite re-requests the old URL every 30 s or less forever and never raises OnClosed; with Default it spends all retries.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 4.1; RFC 9110 15.4

## Suggested fix
Treat redirect statuses as permanent while redirects are not followed, and surface the status and Location to the application.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 3xx handshake responses are treated as permanent failures and stop the reconnect loop.
- [ ] The failure surfaced to the application includes the status code and the Location header.
- [ ] OnClosed is raised after a 3xx rejection under every reconnect policy.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ serves a 301 with Location and asserts no retry and OnClosed with the status and fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] ResilientWebSocketClient caches metrics and health snapshots in plain multi-word struct fields shared across threads
body:
## Summary
The latest metrics and health snapshots are stored in plain struct fields written by callback threads and read by getters. A read during a reconnect can return a mix of two updates, and a 64-bit counter can tear on 32-bit IL2CPP (armv7). The inner WebSocketMetricsCollector uses a lock to avoid this.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:712`

## Problem
_latestMetrics (WebSocketMetrics: eleven longs and two TimeSpans) and _latestHealth are plain struct fields (:34-35) written from child-connection callback threads (:712-713, :721) and from the connect path (:369-370), and read by the Metrics/Health getters on user threads whenever _client is null, i.e. during every reconnect (:77, :86). _receivePumpTask, _incomingQueue and _lifecycleCts are likewise read and written across threads without Volatile (:334, :372, :678-682, :696).

**Failure scenario.** Polling client.Metrics from the main thread during a reconnect can return a snapshot mixing two updates; on 32-bit IL2CPP (armv7) a single 64-bit counter can be torn. The inner WebSocketMetricsCollector takes a lock precisely to avoid this (WebSocketMetricsCollector.cs:8).

## Suggested fix
Store the latest snapshots as immutable reference objects swapped with Volatile.Write (or guard them with _sync), and read the task, queue and CTS fields through Volatile or under _sync.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Snapshots are immutable reference objects swapped with Volatile.Write, or all accesses are guarded by _sync.
- [ ] Task, queue and CTS fields are read through Volatile or under _sync.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ hammers Metrics and Health getters from several threads during reconnects and asserts each snapshot is internally consistent and fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketClient.Create(options) inspects only ReconnectPolicy and discards the options
body:
## Summary
Create reads the reconnect policy from the options to choose a client type and then drops them, so the same options must be passed again to ConnectAsync. If they are omitted, the client connects with defaults: no compression and no reconnect policy, so the first disconnect ends the connection without an error. The documented usage is therefore silently wrong.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:46`

## Problem
Create clones and validates `options` into the local `effective`, uses it for `effective.ReconnectPolicy.Enabled` and drops it (WebSocketClient.cs:50-58); neither client constructor takes options. ConnectAsync(Uri) builds `new WebSocketConnectionOptions()` (WebSocketClient.cs:99, ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:92). ResilientWebSocketClient reads its policy from the ConnectAsync options (`_options?.ReconnectPolicy`, :563); WebSocketClient.ConnectAsync throws InvalidOperationException when the ConnectAsync options enable reconnect (112-116). The reconnect policy is a client-selection concern stored on WebSocketConnectionOptions, which WebSocketConnection itself ignores. OnReconnecting/OnReconnected exist only on the concrete ResilientWebSocketClient (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:43-44) although Create returns IWebSocketClient; the docs need a downcast (Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:147) and pass `options` twice (:153).

**Failure scenario.** `var ws = WebSocketClient.Create(new WebSocketConnectionOptions().WithReconnection(WebSocketReconnectPolicy.Default).WithCompression()); await ws.ConnectAsync(uri);` returns a ResilientWebSocketClient that connects with default options: no compression, policy None, so the first disconnect closes it without any reconnect and without an error. The opposite order (Create() then ConnectAsync(uri, optionsWithReconnect)) throws InvalidOperationException at connect time.

## Suggested fix
Bind options to the client at construction (constructors and Create keep the validated clone; ConnectAsync(uri) uses it, as UHttpClient does with UHttpClientOptions), or drop the options parameter from Create and select the client explicitly. Expose reconnect notifications without a downcast (an IResilientWebSocketClient interface or events on IWebSocketClient).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Options are validated, cloned and bound to the client at construction; ConnectAsync(uri) uses them.
- [ ] Create(options) followed by ConnectAsync(uri) honours compression and reconnect policy.
- [ ] Public API change has XML docs; documentation examples match the behaviour.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ creates a client with compression and a reconnect policy, calls ConnectAsync(uri) and asserts the negotiated extension and reconnect behaviour and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Create clones/validates options into a local, reads only ReconnectPolicy.Enabled and drops it (WebSocketClient.cs:50-58); neither client stores constructor options. ConnectAsync(Uri) uses new WebSocketConnectionOptions() (WebSocketClient.cs:99, ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:92); the resilient client takes its policy from the ConnectAsync options (:114, :563), and WebSocketClient.ConnectAsync throws InvalidOperationException for reconnect-enabled options (:112-116). The docs do cast and pass options twice (Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:147, 153). One correction to the scenario: on the first disconnect the resilient client does raise OnError (RaiseError at :561) before closing, so it is not entirely 'without an error'; no reconnect and no compression are as stated. #121 (API configuration review) covers UHttpClientOptions, not this.

Also reported as `docs-accuracy-04` (merged into this issue).

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketClient.Create() throws ArgumentNullException when no transport is passed and reconnect is not enabled
body:
## Summary
With no transport argument and no reconnect policy, Create() passes a null transport to the plain client constructor and throws ArgumentNullException before any connect. This is the documented default path, also used by UHttpClient.WebSocket and the UnityWebSocketClient component with Auto Reconnect off. The WebSocket feature is unusable through its factory unless a reconnect policy is set.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:58`

## Problem
Create(options = null, transport = null) ends with `return new WebSocketClient(transport);` (WebSocketClient.cs:58). The only one-argument constructor is `WebSocketClient(IWebSocketTransport transport) { _providedTransport = transport ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(transport)); }` (WebSocketClient.cs:41-44), so a null transport throws. Only the reconnect branch (lines 53-56) checks `transport != null` and falls back to the parameterless constructor. Callers that pass no transport: Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:39 (`WebSocketClient.Create(options)` with ReconnectPolicy None built at :44-54), Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketClient.cs:394 (reconnect only when `_autoReconnect`, a bool defaulting to false, :574), and the quick start in Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:13. No test calls WebSocketClient.Create (rg over Tests/ finds none; the Unity tests inject ClientFactory, the autobahn/soak/player-smoke tools use `new WebSocketClient()`).

**Failure scenario.** `IWebSocketClient ws = WebSocketClient.Create(new WebSocketConnectionOptions());` (docs line 13), `await httpClient.WebSocket(uri)`, or a UnityWebSocketClient component with Auto Reconnect unchecked -> ArgumentNullException("transport") before any connect; the feature is unusable through its factory unless a reconnect policy is set.

## Suggested fix
Return `transport != null ? new WebSocketClient(transport) : new WebSocketClient()` (mirroring the resilient branch) and add a test that Create() with default options connects through the registered factory, plus one through UHttpClient.WebSocket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create() with default options and no transport returns a WebSocketClient built with the default constructor and connects through the registered factory.
- [ ] UHttpClient.WebSocket(uri) connects with default options.
- [ ] UnityWebSocketClient with Auto Reconnect unchecked connects.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ calls Create() with default options and connects, and a second test through UHttpClient.WebSocket and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Create(options, transport = null) falls through to `return new WebSocketClient(transport);` (WebSocketClient.cs:58); the only one-argument constructor throws ArgumentNullException on null (:41-44). Only the reconnect branch checks transport != null (:53-56). Default ReconnectPolicy is None (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:129). Callers with no transport: UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:39 (UHttpClient.WebSocket, options built without reconnect :44-54), UnityWebSocketClient.cs:394 (reconnect only when _autoReconnect, :574), and the quick start (Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:13, 27). rg over Tests/, Samples~ and Tools~ finds no call of WebSocketClient.Create or of the .WebSocket( extension, so nothing exercises the path; the line dates from the initial phase-18 commit (6ccfab5). No guard, no issue (open or closed) found.

title: [WebSocket] ReceiveAllAsync takes its exclusivity flag when called and releases it only when an enumerator is disposed
body:
## Summary
The exclusivity flag is acquired when ReceiveAllAsync is called, not when enumeration starts. If the returned stream is never enumerated, the flag is never released and every later ReceiveAsync or ReceiveAllAsync on that client throws InvalidOperationException for its lifetime, across reconnects.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:255`

## Problem
`Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref _receiveAllInProgress, 1, 0)` runs in ReceiveAllAsync itself (WebSocketClient.cs:255; ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:185); the flag is cleared only by the enumerator's DisposeAsync through the onDispose callback (WebSocketAsyncEnumerable.cs:90-97). Nothing else resets it, including ConnectAsync. GetAsyncEnumerator may be called more than once on the returned object, and the first enumerator's disposal clears the flag while a second is still active. Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClientTests.cs:198-203 asserts that the second ReceiveAllAsync call throws at call time.

**Failure scenario.** `var stream = client.ReceiveAllAsync(ct);` is created but never enumerated (an early return, an exception before the `await foreach`, or a lazy pipeline that is dropped): every later ReceiveAsync and ReceiveAllAsync on that client throws InvalidOperationException for the rest of its life, across reconnects.

## Suggested fix
Acquire the flag in GetAsyncEnumerator (IAsyncEnumerable is expected to be lazy) and release it in DisposeAsync; reject a second concurrent enumerator there.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The flag is acquired in GetAsyncEnumerator and released in DisposeAsync.
- [ ] A second concurrent enumerator is rejected at GetAsyncEnumerator.
- [ ] Creating ReceiveAllAsync without enumerating does not block later receive calls.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ creates an un-enumerated ReceiveAllAsync stream and asserts a later ReceiveAsync succeeds and fails before the fix

## Context

title: [WebSocket] Every message is copied to a fresh byte[] when OnMessage has a subscriber, while the pooled original sits in an unread pull queue
body:
## Summary
With an OnMessage subscriber, WebSocketClient and ResilientWebSocketClient call PublishDroppingOldest, which allocates a detached byte[] copy of every message and also parks the pooled original in the pull queue. The queue keeps up to 100 messages or 8 MB of pooled buffers rented although no ReceiveAsync consumer exists. UnityWebSocketBridge always subscribes OnMessage, so every Unity event-driven client pays this per message.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:429`

## Problem
With a subscriber every message goes through PublishDroppingOldest (WebSocketClient.cs:429, :466-483; ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:419): WebSocketMessage.CreateDetachedCopy allocates 'new byte[length]' and copies the payload (WebSocketMessage.cs:99-100), and the pooled original is pushed into the pull queue with drop-oldest (WebSocketClient.cs:474), where it stays until 100 newer messages or 8 MB displace it (WebSocketConstants.cs:28-31). Text messages were already decoded to a string in the receive loop (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:274-276). UnityWebSocketBridge subscribes OnMessage (Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:59), so this is the default Unity path. The retention is documented (IWebSocketClient.cs:23-28); the per-message copy is not needed for it.

**Failure scenario.** An event-driven client receiving 4 KB text messages at 50 per second allocates for each a 4 KB byte[] that handlers reading Text never touch, on top of the 8 KB string, and keeps the last 100 pooled buffers (up to 8 MB per client) rented for a pull consumer that does not exist.

## Suggested fix
Hand the handler the pooled message and return it after the callback (or copy only when a handler keeps it), and feed the pull queue only once a ReceiveAsync/ReceiveAllAsync consumer has shown up.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Handlers of OnMessage receive the message without an unconditional per-message byte[] copy (allocations per message for a text message that is only read as Text drop to the decoded string).
- [ ] The pull queue is fed only once a ReceiveAsync/ReceiveAllAsync consumer exists; with only an OnMessage subscriber no pooled buffer stays rented after the callback returns.
- [ ] A handler that keeps the message still gets valid data (copy on retention, documented in IWebSocketClient).
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ asserts ByteArrayPool active count and allocation behaviour with an OnMessage-only subscriber and fails before the fix.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-13` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. With a subscriber the listener calls PublishDroppingOldest (WebSocketClient.cs:429): CreateDetachedCopy allocates new byte[length] and copies (WebSocketMessage.cs:99-100) even for text messages whose string was already decoded (SendReceive.cs:274-276), then the pooled original goes to the pull queue with drop-oldest (:474) and stays rented until displaced (100 messages / 8 MB, WebSocketConstants.cs:28-31) or the client closes. ResilientWebSocketClient does the same (:419). UnityWebSocketBridge always subscribes OnMessage (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:59), so this is the Unity default path. The retention is documented (IWebSocketClient.cs:23-28, #78) but nothing checks whether a pull consumer exists, and the copy is unconditional. No open issue.
