title: [WebSocket] SendAsync on a closed or reconnecting client throws InvalidOperationException instead of WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed)
body:
## Summary
WebSocketClient.SendAsync and ResilientWebSocketClient.RequireOpenClient pre-check the state and throw InvalidOperationException for any state other than Open, so the connection's own mapping (WebSocketException with the close status for Closing/Closed) is only reached in a race. After the peer or network closes the connection, or during auto-reconnect, callers get a usage-error type they cannot tell from a programming error. This contradicts the error model and a test pins the wrong behaviour.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:569`

## Problem
WebSocketConnection deliberately fails sends on a closing/closed connection with WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed) carrying the close status, 'whichever side of a concurrent abort, pong timeout or close the send lands on' (ThrowIfCannotSend, SendReceive.cs:814-835, #84). WebSocketClient.SendAsync first runs EnsureOpenState, which throws InvalidOperationException for any state other than Open (WebSocketClient.cs:569-577), so the connection's mapping is reached only when the close lands between the check and the send. ResilientWebSocketClient.RequireOpenClient throws InvalidOperationException whenever the child is not Open, including the whole reconnect window (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:664-674). Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClientTests.cs:97-113 (SendAfterClose_ThrowsInvalidOperationException) asserts the pre-check behaviour.

**Failure scenario.** The peer or the network closes the connection; the application's next SendAsync throws InvalidOperationException("SendAsync requires Open state. Current state: Closed.") instead of a UHttpException, so `catch (WebSocketException)`/`catch (UHttpException)` handlers and retry logic miss it, and the same failure yields a different exception type depending on a race. During auto-reconnect every send fails with a usage-error type the caller cannot distinguish from a programming error.

## Suggested fix
Keep InvalidOperationException for None/Connecting-before-first-connect only; for Closing/Closed and for the resilient client's reconnect window throw WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed) with the close status (drop the pre-check and let the connection decide). Update the test to the error-model rule.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SendAsync in Closing/Closed state and during the resilient client's reconnect window throws WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed) carrying the close status.
- [ ] InvalidOperationException remains only for None and Connecting-before-first-connect.
- [ ] SendAfterClose_ThrowsInvalidOperationException in Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClientTests.cs is updated to the new contract, and a deterministic NUnit test for the reconnect window is added under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ and fails before the fix.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WebSocketClient.SendAsync calls EnsureOpenState first (WebSocketClient.cs:217, 224), which throws InvalidOperationException for any state other than Open (:569-577), so the connection's deliberate mapping (ThrowIfCannotSend, SendReceive.cs:814-835: None/Connecting = InvalidOperationException, Closing/Closed = WebSocketException, #84) is reached only when the close lands after the pre-check. ResilientWebSocketClient.RequireOpenClient throws InvalidOperationException whenever the child is null or not Open, including the reconnect window (:664-674). The test SendAfterClose_ThrowsInvalidOperationException pins the pre-check (WebSocketClientTests.cs:96-113), but only for a close the application itself made; no doc comment on IWebSocketClient.SendAsync (IWebSocketClient.cs:68-75) states the contract. The exception type for a peer/network close therefore depends on a race.

title: [WebSocket] Typed-message SendAsync<T> round-trips UTF-8 through a string and IWebSocketMessageSerializer is loosely typed and bound to the global JSON serializer
body:
## Summary
For text serializers SendAsync<T> decodes the serializer's UTF-8 bytes to a string only for IWebSocketClient.SendAsync(string) to encode them again, although WebSocketConnection already has SendTextAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>). IWebSocketMessageSerializer.MessageType is typed WebSocketOpcode, which admits opcodes rejected at run time, and JsonWebSocketSerializer<T> always uses the process-wide JSON serializer. Games sending frequent JSON updates allocate extra arrays and strings per message and cannot configure JSON separately for the socket protocol.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClientExtensions.cs:24`

## Problem
IWebSocketMessageSerializer<T>.Serialize returns ReadOnlyMemory<byte> (IWebSocketMessageSerializer.cs:9). For text serializers SendAsync<T> decodes those bytes back to a string (`StrictUtf8.GetString(payload.Span)`, WebSocketClientExtensions.cs:29-31) because IWebSocketClient only offers SendAsync(string) for text (IWebSocketClient.cs:69), and WebSocketConnection.SendTextAsync then encodes the string again into a pooled buffer (SendReceive.cs:14-54). With JsonWebSocketSerializer the chain is object -> JSON string -> byte[] (JsonWebSocketSerializer.cs:52-57) -> string -> pooled bytes: two extra allocations proportional to the message and three transcoding passes per send. WebSocketConnection already has SendTextAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> utf8Payload) (SendReceive.cs:56-59) but the interface does not expose it. `MessageType` is typed WebSocketOpcode (IWebSocketMessageSerializer.cs:7), admitting Continuation/Close/Ping/Pong that SendAsync<T> rejects at run time with ArgumentException (:51-53), although WebSocketMessageType exists. JsonWebSocketSerializer<T> has no constructor taking a serializer and is constrained to `class` (JsonWebSocketSerializer.cs:33-34): it always uses the process-wide bridge/JsonSerializer.Default shared with the HTTP client, and compiles without TurboHTTP.JSON but fails at run time with SerializationFailed when no bridge is registered.

**Failure scenario.** A game sending 30 JSON state updates per second of 2 KB each allocates roughly an extra 2 KB byte[] and a 4 KB string per message that go straight to the GC, on top of the JSON string; a project that needs a different JSON configuration for its socket protocol than for REST must change the global default.

## Suggested fix
Add a UTF-8 text send to IWebSocketClient (or an internal fast path the extension can reach) so serializers' bytes go to the wire once; type MessageType as WebSocketMessageType; let JsonWebSocketSerializer<T> take an optional serializer instance and write into a pooled IBufferWriter<byte>.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] IWebSocketClient (or an internal fast path) exposes a UTF-8 text send so serializer bytes reach the wire without a string round trip; allocations per typed send are reduced and the figure is recorded in the PR.
- [ ] IWebSocketMessageSerializer.MessageType is typed WebSocketMessageType.
- [ ] JsonWebSocketSerializer<T> accepts an optional serializer instance.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ verifies the bytes sent and that no string transcoding occurs for text serializers.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-19` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. IWebSocketMessageSerializer<T>.Serialize returns ReadOnlyMemory<byte> (IWebSocketMessageSerializer.cs:9); for Text, SendAsync<T> decodes it to a string (WebSocketClientExtensions.cs:24-41) because IWebSocketClient has only SendAsync(string) for text (IWebSocketClient.cs:68-75); WebSocketClient.SendAsync(string) calls SendTextAsync(string), which re-encodes into a pooled buffer (WebSocketClient.cs:210-219, WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:14-54). JsonWebSocketSerializer adds object -> JSON string -> byte[] before that (JsonWebSocketSerializer.cs:52-57), so each typed text send allocates one byte[] and one string beyond the JSON string and transcodes three times, although the connection already has SendTextAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>) (SendReceive.cs:56-59) that the interface does not expose. MessageType is WebSocketOpcode (IWebSocketMessageSerializer.cs:7) and other opcodes fail only at run time, after Serialize already ran (WebSocketClientExtensions.cs:51-53). JsonWebSocketSerializer<T> is `where T : class`, has no constructor and always goes through ProjectJsonBridge (JsonWebSocketSerializer.cs:33-34, :52, :84), failing with SerializationFailed when no bridge is registered (documented, :44-47). No guard or alternative path exists; the allocation is per message on an opt-in convenience API, on a GC-sensitive runtime. Not covered by #120 (HTTP hot paths only).

Also reported as `ws-runtime-25` (merged into this issue).

Related: [[R11-ws-runtime-26]].

title: [WebSocket] ReceiveAllAsync<T> awaits the inner enumeration without ConfigureAwait(false) and passes the token twice
body:
## Summary
ReceiveAllAsync<T> in WebSocketClientExtensions is the only await in the module without ConfigureAwait(false), and it passes the same token to ReceiveAllAsync and WithCancellation, which makes WebSocketAsyncEnumerable allocate a linked source of the token with itself. On the Unity main thread each message continuation is posted to the synchronization context inside the library iterator.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClientExtensions.cs:81`

## Problem
`await foreach (var raw in client.ReceiveAllAsync(ct).WithCancellation(ct))` (WebSocketClientExtensions.cs:81) has no `.ConfigureAwait(false)`; every other await in Runtime/WebSocket and Runtime/WebSocket.Transport uses it. `ct` is also passed twice (to ReceiveAllAsync and WithCancellation), which makes WebSocketAsyncEnumerable.GetAsyncEnumerator allocate a linked source of the same token with itself (WebSocketAsyncEnumerable.cs:32-36).

**Failure scenario.** Called from the Unity main thread, each message's MoveNextAsync continuation is posted to UnitySynchronizationContext inside the library iterator and then again by the caller's own await, adding a frame of latency per message and running deserialization on the main thread even for callers that wanted background processing.

## Suggested fix
Use `.WithCancellation(ct).ConfigureAwait(false)` and pass the token once.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The enumeration uses WithCancellation(ct).ConfigureAwait(false) and the token is passed once.
- [ ] No linked cancellation source is allocated when the same token is used.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ checks the continuation does not run on a captured SynchronizationContext and fails before the fix.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-21` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: best-practices.

title: [WebSocket] User event handlers run unguarded in FinalizeClose and other critical sections, so one throwing handler leaves the connection half-finalized with its socket open
body:
## Summary
FinalizeClose sets _finalized and then raises Error and StateChanged before it completes the close source, the queues and the stream disposal, and WebSocketClient forwards these straight to user delegates without try/catch. A throwing OnError/OnClosed handler therefore leaves the state Open, the receive queue uncompleted and the socket allocated, and later Dispose is a no-op. OnConnected, OnReconnecting and MetricsUpdated have the same exposure, so a throwing OnReconnecting handler silently stops reconnection. Only OnMessage is isolated.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:111`

## Problem
FinalizeClose sets `_finalized` (Lifecycle.cs:101) and then invokes `Error` (110-111) before it resolves `_remoteCloseTcs`, cancels the keep-alive/lifecycle sources, completes `_receiveQueue`, moves the state to Closed or disposes the stream (114-157); the later state transition invokes `StateChanged` (81-82) before TrackAbandonedReceiveLoop/SafeDispose(stream)/ReleaseResources (155-157). WebSocketClient forwards both straight to user delegates with no try/catch: HandleConnectionError -> OnError (WebSocketClient.cs:529-536), HandleConnectionStateChanged -> RaiseClosedFromConnection -> OnClosed (510-560). Because `_finalized` is already 1, every later FinalizeClose/Abort/Dispose returns at line 101-102 and the stream is never disposed. Same pattern elsewhere: MetricsUpdated is raised inside the receive loop and inside the send funnel (TryPublishMetricsUpdate, Lifecycle.cs:267-268, called from Extensions.cs:70), where a throwing handler is mapped to SendFailed and aborts the connection after a successful send (SendReceive.cs:623-646); OnConnected is raised at the end of ConnectAsync (WebSocketClient.cs:206-207) so a throw reports a failed connect while the socket and listener stay alive; OnReconnecting/OnError are raised inside RunReconnectLoopAsync (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:561, 571-572), where a throw ends reconnection without completing the queue or raising OnClosed. Only OnMessage is isolated (RaiseMessage). The HTTP side's contract (architecture.md, handler callbacks) requires a throwing callback to leave every completion source resolved.

**Failure scenario.** A plain WebSocketClient user subscribes OnError and touches a Unity API from it (the event is raised on a pool thread, so UnityException is thrown), or simply has a bug in the handler. The network drops: FinalizeClose throws out of the receive loop after `_finalized = 1`; State stays Open, ReceiveAsync never completes, the socket and receive buffers stay allocated, and Dispose() is a no-op for the stream. With a throwing OnReconnecting handler the resilient client silently stops reconnecting and pull consumers hang.

## Suggested fix
Finish all internal teardown first and raise events last, each invocation wrapped so a handler fault cannot abort teardown (route it to a diagnostics sink); never raise user events inside the send funnel or the receive loop's try block. Add tests with throwing OnError/OnClosed/OnConnected/OnMetricsUpdated/OnReconnecting handlers asserting Closed state, completed queues and a disposed stream.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All user-facing events (OnError, OnClosed, OnConnected, OnReconnecting, StateChanged, metrics events) are raised inside try/catch and after the connection's cleanup is complete or outside critical sections; a throwing handler cannot skip finalization.
- [ ] After a throwing OnError handler and a network drop the state becomes Closed, ReceiveAsync completes and the stream is disposed.
- [ ] A throwing OnReconnecting handler does not stop the reconnect loop or leave pull consumers hanging.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit tests under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ with throwing handlers for each event fail before the fix.

WebSocketClient.HandleConnectionError invokes OnError with no try/catch (WebSocketClient.cs:529-536); a throw leaves State Open, the queue uncompleted and the stream undisposed, and every later Abort/Dispose/FinalizeClose returns at :101-102 (AbortCore only calls FinalizeClose, :59-70; the transport's Dispose only sets a flag, RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:281-284). title: [WebSocket] WebSocketConnection never drains its receive queue, so queued messages at Dispose, Abort or close never return their pooled buffers
body:
## Summary
FinalizeClose completes the connection's receive queue but neither it nor Dispose drains it, and the owning client cancels its listener before closing the connection. Messages still queued (up to 100 or 8 MB) become unreachable and their ByteArrayPool buffers are never returned. ByteArrayPool.ActiveCount, the leak oracle of the soak harness, drifts upward on every such close.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:120`

## Problem
FinalizeClose completes _receiveQueue (:120) but neither it nor Dispose/DisposeAsync (:17-57) drains it; BoundedAsyncQueue.Drain is called only for the client-level queues (WebSocketClient.cs:683-690, ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:694-702). After Dispose, ReceiveAsync throws ObjectDisposedException (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:68), so the queued WebSocketMessage objects are unreachable. WebSocketClient.Dispose/DisposeAsync cancel the listener before closing the connection (WebSocketClient.cs:341, :364) and CloseAsync cancels it right after (:326), so whatever is still in the connection queue is abandoned.

**Failure scenario.** Disposing or closing a client with a backlog leaves up to 100 messages / 8 MB of ByteArrayPool buffers that are never returned: the arrays go to the GC, and ByteArrayPool's ActiveCount (the #292 leak oracle of the soak harness) drifts upward on every such close.

## Suggested fix
Drain and dispose the remaining messages when the connection is disposed and when the owning client stops its listener, as the client queues already do.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Messages remaining in the connection receive queue are drained and disposed on Dispose, DisposeAsync, Abort and client close.
- [ ] ByteArrayPool active count returns to its baseline after closing or disposing a client with a queued backlog.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ closes a connection with queued messages and asserts the pool count; it fails before the fix.

title: [WebSocket] MetricsUpdated and ConnectionQualityChanged run inline under the message lock and on the receive loop, and their exceptions abort a healthy connection
body:
## Summary
TryPublishMetricsUpdate raises MetricsUpdated and the health monitor raises ConnectionQualityChanged synchronously from the receive loop, the keep-alive loop and the send path while the message lock is held. A throwing handler is treated as a transport failure: the receive loop finalizes with ReceiveFailed, and a send that already succeeded is reported as failed and aborts the connection. A slow handler blocks pongs, close processing and every other sender.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:268`

## Problem
TryPublishMetricsUpdate (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:250-269) invokes MetricsUpdated and, through WebSocketHealthMonitor (WebSocketHealthMonitor.cs:82-83, :120-121), ConnectionQualityChanged synchronously. It is called from the receive loop (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:309, :397, :423), from the send path while _messageLock is held (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:70, under SendReceive.cs:611-621), from the Close frame send (:602) and from the keep-alive loop (:983). WebSocketClient forwards to user handlers unguarded (WebSocketClient.cs:540-541, :546-547). The exceptions land in the transport-failure handlers: the receive loop's catch-all (SendReceive.cs:370-376) and the send filter (:627-646).

**Failure scenario.** A throwing OnMetricsUpdated or OnConnectionQualityChanged handler aborts a healthy connection: in the receive loop it becomes FinalizeClose(AbnormalClosure, ReceiveFailed); after a message was fully written it becomes 'Unexpected error while sending message; the connection was aborted'. A slow handler blocks the receive loop (no pong replies, no close processing) or every other sender, because it runs under _messageLock. With the defaults (every 100 messages or 5 s) this is on the hot paths of every subscriber.

## Suggested fix
Raise diagnostics events outside the locks and outside the I/O try blocks, wrapped in try/catch, so they can neither fail nor stall the connection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Diagnostics events are raised outside _messageLock and outside the I/O try blocks, wrapped in try/catch.
- [ ] A throwing OnMetricsUpdated or OnConnectionQualityChanged handler does not fail a send, abort the connection or end the receive loop.
- [ ] A slow handler does not hold the message lock.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ with a throwing handler fails before the fix.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described. TryPublishMetricsUpdate invokes MetricsUpdated synchronously (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:267-268) and WebSocketHealthMonitor raises OnQualityChanged synchronously (WebSocketHealthMonitor.cs:82-83, :120-121); WebSocketClient forwards unguarded (WebSocketClient.cs:540-541, :546-547). Call sites: receive loop (SendReceive.cs:309, :397, :420-423), send path under _messageLock (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:70 inside SendReceive.cs:611-621), Close send (:602), keep-alive loop (:983). A handler exception in the receive loop lands in the catch-all (:370-376) as FinalizeClose(AbnormalClosure, ReceiveFailed); after a fully written message it matches the send filter (:627-630) and becomes SendFailed with the connection aborted. Severity lowered to low: it needs a throwing or slow user diagnostics handler, the outcome is a clean abort reported through OnError with the handler exception as inner exception (not a wedge like ws-runtime-01), the Unity bridge dispatches these handlers guarded, and synchronous event delivery is ordinary .NET behaviour. Still worth guarding together with ws-runtime-01/06.

title: [WebSocket] PrefetchedStream stays in the read path for the connection's life and its byte[] ReadAsync override is an async method
body:
## Summary
When the handshake read picked up bytes past the 101 response, the stream is wrapped in PrefetchedStream permanently. Its ReadAsync(byte[], int, int, CancellationToken) override, which the frame reader uses, is an async method, so every later read allocates a state machine and a Task<int>. This affects servers that send a first message in the same segment as the 101.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:480`

## Problem
When the handshake read picked up bytes past the 101 response, the connection stream is wrapped in PrefetchedStream for its whole life (WebSocketConnection.cs:284-287). Its ReadAsync(byte[], int, int, CancellationToken) override, the overload the frame reader uses (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:299), is an async method (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:480-490), so after the prefetched bytes are consumed every read still allocates a state machine and a Task<int> on top of the inner stream's.

**Failure scenario.** A server that sends its first message in the same segment as the 101 (greeting, subscription snapshot) puts every later frame read of that connection (2-3 per frame) through an extra async state machine and Task allocation.

## Suggested fix
Make the override non-async: Task.FromResult for prefetched data and the inner task directly otherwise, or unwrap the stream once the prefetched bytes are consumed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PrefetchedStream.ReadAsync(byte[]...) is not async: it returns Task.FromResult for prefetched data and the inner task otherwise (or the stream is unwrapped after the prefetched bytes are consumed).
- [ ] Reads after the prefetched bytes are consumed add no allocation beyond the inner stream's; the measured figure is recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ covers prefetched bytes followed by inner reads and asserts the data and allocation behaviour.

title: [WebSocket] A send runs through eight to nine nested async Task methods, several pure pass-throughs, with no synchronous fast path
body:
## Summary
A send passes through ResilientWebSocketClient, WebSocketClient, SendTextAsync/SendBinaryAsync, SendMessageAsync, the extension write, WriteMessageFramesAsync, WriteFrameLockedAsync, WebSocketFrameWriter and TryWriteSmallFrameSingleWriteAsync, each an async Task method. When the stream write does not complete synchronously, as is normal for NetworkStream and SslStream on Mono and IL2CPP, each layer allocates a state machine and Task, roughly 1-2 KB per small message.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:61`

## Problem
A send passes through ResilientWebSocketClient.SendAsync (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:146-159), WebSocketClient.SendAsync (WebSocketClient.cs:221-227), SendBinaryAsync/SendTextAsync (SendReceive.cs:56-64, pass-through async methods), SendMessageAsync (:605), WriteMessageWithExtensionsAsync (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:13), WriteMessageFramesAsync (SendReceive.cs:662), WriteFrameLockedAsync (:711), WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteFrameAsync (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:244) and TryWriteSmallFrameSingleWriteAsync (:337, async Task<bool>).

**Failure scenario.** Whenever the stream write does not complete synchronously (the norm for NetworkStream and SslStream on Mono and IL2CPP) each layer boxes its state machine and allocates a Task: on the order of 1-2 KB of garbage per small message sent.

## Suggested fix
Return the inner task directly from the pass-through methods, fold the small-frame helper into WriteFrameAsync, and use ValueTask on the internal layers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pass-through methods return the inner task directly and the small-frame helper is folded into WriteFrameAsync; internal layers use ValueTask where appropriate.
- [ ] Allocations per small text message send are measured before and after and the reduction is recorded in the PR.

title: [WebSocket] CloseAsync with a reason that is not UTF-8 encodable leaves the connection in Closing with no Close frame sent
body:
## Summary
CloseAsync validates only the status code. CloseCoreAsync moves the state to Closing and sets _closeFrameSent before the frame is built, and WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteCloseAsync then throws ArgumentException for a reason containing a lone surrogate. The exception escapes, sends are refused and no Close frame is sent; a second CloseAsync skips the frame and ends with timeout and 1006. This happens for example when a user string truncated by Substring splits an emoji.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:133`

## Problem
CloseAsync validates only the code (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:102-107). CloseCoreAsync moves Open to Closing (133) and SendCloseFrameIfNeededAsync sets _closeFrameSent = 1 (575) before the frame is built. WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteCloseAsync throws ArgumentException for a reason with a lone surrogate (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:149-158); the filter in WriteFrameLockedAsync excludes ArgumentException (766) and CloseCoreAsync catches only OperationCanceledException (146-155), so the exception escapes.

**Failure scenario.** `CloseAsync(NormalClosure, userText.Substring(0, 60))` where the cut splits an emoji throws ArgumentException. The state is Closing, sends are refused and no Close frame went out; a second CloseAsync skips the frame (flag already set), waits CloseHandshakeTimeout and aborts with 1006.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 5.5.1

## Suggested fix
Validate (or encode) the reason in CloseAsync before any state change, with the same check the WebSocketCloseStatus constructor uses.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CloseAsync validates the reason (same check as the WebSocketCloseStatus constructor, including the 123-byte limit of RFC 6455 5.5.1) before any state change and throws ArgumentException without altering state.
- [ ] After the rejected call the connection stays Open and a subsequent valid CloseAsync completes the closing handshake.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ with a lone-surrogate reason fails before the fix.

title: [WebSocket] CloseHandshakeTimeout = TimeSpan.Zero means cancel immediately on a local close but no limit on a peer-initiated close
body:
## Summary
CloseCoreAsync applies CancelAfter(zero) unconditionally so a local close aborts at once, while HandleControlFrameAsync and AwaitServerTransportCloseAsync treat zero as no timeout or skip. Validate accepts zero and the property documentation does not define it. Other options (PingInterval, PongTimeout, IdleTimeout) use zero for no limit, and DisposeAsync uses a hard-coded 1 s budget regardless of the option.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:137`

## Problem
CloseCoreAsync calls `timeoutCts.CancelAfter(_options.CloseHandshakeTimeout)` unconditionally (SendReceive.cs:136-137), so zero cancels the Close send/wait at once and the method aborts (157-161). HandleControlFrameAsync arms the reply timeout only `if (_options.CloseHandshakeTimeout > TimeSpan.Zero)` (444-446) and AwaitServerTransportCloseAsync returns immediately for `timeout <= TimeSpan.Zero` (537-539). Validate allows zero (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:219-220) and the property has a one-line summary. DisposeAsync additionally uses a hard-coded 1 s budget regardless of the option (Lifecycle.cs:29, 44).

**Failure scenario.** A caller sets CloseHandshakeTimeout to zero expecting 'do not time out' (the meaning PingInterval, PongTimeout and IdleTimeout give zero): CloseAsync aborts the connection, usually before the Close frame is written, and the peer records an abnormal closure; a peer-initiated close on the same connection waits without bound for the reply write.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 7.1.2

## Suggested fix
Define zero once (either reject it in Validate or treat it as 'no handshake wait' consistently in all three places) and document it; derive the DisposeAsync budget from the option.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Zero is defined once, either rejected in WebSocketConnectionOptions.Validate or treated as the same behaviour in all three places, and documented in the XML docs.
- [ ] DisposeAsync derives its budget from CloseHandshakeTimeout instead of the hard-coded 1 s.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ covers local close and peer-initiated close with zero timeout and fails before the fix.

title: [WebSocket] CloseAsync cannot finish the closing handshake while the receive loop is parked on a full delivery queue and ends with an abnormal 1006 closure
body:
## Summary
When the delivery queue is full the receive loop waits in EnqueueWhileParkedAsync and does not read the socket, so the peer's Close reply is never seen. CloseCoreAsync waits for the remote close until CloseHandshakeTimeout and then aborts with status 1006 and an Error event, even if the server answered at once. A pull consumer that stops reading a busy stream and then calls CloseAsync takes the full timeout.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:144`

## Problem
When the queue is full the loop waits in EnqueueWhileParkedAsync (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:903-915) and does not read the socket. CloseCoreAsync sends the Close and waits for _remoteCloseTcs (143-144), which is set only when the loop reads the peer's Close (431) or by FinalizeClose. Nothing unparks or drains the loop on a local close, so the wait ends at CloseHandshakeTimeout with AbortCore (157-160): status 1006 and an Error event. WebSocketClient's pull-only listener blocks the same way on its own queue (WebSocketClient.cs:415).

**Failure scenario.** A pull consumer stops calling ReceiveAsync on a busy stream until both queues are full (100 messages or 8 MB each) and then calls CloseAsync. The call takes the full 5 s and ends with OnError('aborted') and OnClosed(1006), although the server answered the Close at once.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 7.1.2

## Suggested fix
Once a local close has started, stop applying backpressure to data frames (discard them, or enqueue without waiting) so the loop reaches the peer's Close.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Once a local close has started the receive loop stops applying backpressure to data frames (discards or enqueues without waiting) so it reaches the peer's Close frame (RFC 6455 7.1.2).
- [ ] CloseAsync with full queues completes with the peer's close status well before CloseHandshakeTimeout and raises no Error event.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ with full queues and a responsive peer fails before the fix.

title: [WebSocket] Peer TCP close after the client's Close without a Close frame is reported as a clean 1000 closure
body:
## Summary
When the client calls CloseAsync and the server drops the TCP connection without sending its own Close frame, the receive loop sees EOF in the Closing state and finalizes with NormalClosure. The application cannot tell this from a completed closing handshake. RFC 6455 7.1.5 defines this case as an abnormal closure (1006).

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:230`

## Problem
On EOF the reader returns null and the loop does `if (State == WebSocketState.Closing) break;` (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:228-231); then finalStatus = _hasCloseStatus ? _closeStatus : new WebSocketCloseStatus(NormalClosure) and FinalizeClose(finalStatus, null) (321-324). State is Closing at that point only after a local CloseAsync (a received Close leaves the loop through closeFrameReceived). CloseCoreAsync then returns normally with CloseStatus 1000 and no TerminalError (179-183). No test covers a peer that closes TCP without a Close frame after the client's Close.

**Failure scenario.** The client calls CloseAsync(1000); the server or a middlebox FINs without sending a Close frame. OnClosed(NormalClosure, "") is raised, indistinguishable from a completed closing handshake.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 7.1.5

## Suggested fix
On EOF in Closing without a received Close frame, finalize with AbnormalClosure (1006); keep the peer's or the normal status only when closeFrameReceived is true.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] EOF in the Closing state with no received Close frame finalizes with close code 1006 (AbnormalClosure), not 1000
- [ ] When a Close frame was received, the peer's status is still reported
- [ ] OnClosed reports 1006 for the scenario; Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [WebSocket] Oversized or corrupt decompressed messages close with 1002 instead of 1009/1007 and surface as ProtocolViolation
body:
## Summary
Decompression failures and decompressed messages over MaxMessageSize are wrapped into a protocol-error exception with close code 1002. The documentation says a message over the limit after decompression closes with 1009, and every receive-path error reaches the application as WebSocketError.ProtocolViolation.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:334`

## Problem
The catch at WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:334-345 wraps DecompressionFailed and DecompressedMessageTooLarge into WebSocketProtocolException(ProtocolViolation, ..., WebSocketCloseCode.ProtocolError). TryHandleProtocolErrorAsync (506-512) then builds WebSocketException(WebSocketError.ProtocolViolation, ...) for every protocol exception, so InvalidUtf8, MessageTooLarge and FrameTooLarge reach the application only on the inner exception. The MaxMessageSize doc (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:19-24) and Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:121-124 state that a message over the limit after decompression closes with 1009.

**Failure scenario.** A compressed message inflates past MaxMessageSize: the Close frame carries 1002, TerminalError.Error is ProtocolViolation and CloseStatus is 1002. An app or server that distinguishes 'too big' from 'protocol error' gets the wrong class, and the documented 1009 is not what goes on the wire.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 7.4.1

## Suggested fix
Map DecompressedMessageTooLarge to MessageTooBig (1009) and DecompressionFailed to InvalidPayload (1007), and carry the original WebSocketError through TryHandleProtocolErrorAsync.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A decompressed message over MaxMessageSize sends Close 1009 (MessageTooBig) and reports the matching WebSocketError
- [ ] A decompression failure sends Close 1007 (InvalidPayload)
- [ ] The original error class is preserved through TryHandleProtocolErrorAsync for InvalidUtf8, MessageTooLarge and FrameTooLarge

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketConnection close status, terminal error and health monitor are plain fields shared across threads
body:
## Summary
_hasCloseStatus, _closeStatus and _terminalError are plain fields written by the receive loop and FinalizeClose and read from user threads, and _healthMonitor is read twice in a check-then-use while FinalizeClose nulls it. A reader can see the flag with a default struct, mixed code and reason, a stale terminal error on ARM64, or a NullReferenceException in the receive loop.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:432`

## Problem
_hasCloseStatus (bool), _closeStatus (a two-field struct) and _terminalError are plain fields (WebSocketConnection.cs:66-68). The receive loop writes the flag before the value (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:432-433), FinalizeClose writes both from any thread (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:104-105, :109), and CloseStatus, CreateClosedException and ReceiveAsync read them from user threads (WebSocketConnection.cs:142; SendReceive.cs:93-94, :843-844). _healthMonitor is nulled by FinalizeClose (Lifecycle.cs:159-163) while the receive loop reads it twice in a check-then-use (SendReceive.cs:415-420). platform.md requires Interlocked/Volatile for cross-thread fields and int flags instead of bool.

**Failure scenario.** A thread reading CloseStatus while the peer's Close is being recorded can observe the flag set with a default struct (close code 0, null reason) or, with FinalizeClose on another thread, the code of one status with the reason of the other; on ARM64 a reader can also miss a freshly written _terminalError. An Abort() concurrent with a pong makes :420 throw NullReferenceException in the receive loop.

## Suggested fix
Publish the close status as one immutable object through Volatile.Write/Interlocked.CompareExchange, make _terminalError volatile, and read _healthMonitor into a local once.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The close status is published as one immutable object through Volatile.Write or Interlocked.CompareExchange and read with Volatile.Read
- [ ] _terminalError is volatile or accessed through Volatile/Interlocked
- [ ] _healthMonitor is read into a local once in the pong path

title: [WebSocket] A failed or timed-out Close reply overwrites the peer's received close status with 1006
body:
## Summary
After receiving a valid Close frame the client sends the echo; if that write fails or times out, FinalizeClose assigns AbnormalClosure unconditionally and raises Error. A server that closed normally and reset the socket then appears as 1006, and the default reconnect policy reconnects to a server that closed with 1000.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:448`

## Problem
HandleControlFrameAsync records the peer's status (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:431-433) and then sends the reply (448). When that write fails, WriteFrameLockedAsync calls FinalizeClose(new WebSocketCloseStatus(AbnormalClosure), wsEx) (796); FinalizeClose assigns _closeStatus = status unconditionally and raises Error (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:104-112). A reply that times out waiting for _messageLock (replyCts, 444-446) reaches the generic catch at 370-375 with the same result.

**Failure scenario.** A server sends Close(1000) and closes the socket immediately; the client's echo hits a reset. CloseStatus becomes 1006 with SendFailed, OnError fires, and ResilientWebSocketClient's default policy (reconnect on 1006, WebSocketReconnectPolicy.cs:129-134) reconnects to a server that closed normally.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 7.1.5

## Suggested fix
Once a valid Close frame has been received, keep its status as the connection close code and treat a failure to send the echo as non-fatal (finalize with the remote status, no Error). Confirm with a peer that resets right after its Close frame.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Once a valid Close frame was received its status stays the connection close code even if the echo write fails or times out
- [ ] A failed echo is non-fatal and raises no Error

title: [WebSocket] SendAsync encodes, compresses and masks large messages synchronously on the calling thread
body:
## Summary
Text encoding, permessage-deflate and masking of the first chunk run before SendAsync first yields. On the Unity main thread with a large message this blocks the frame, possibly tens of milliseconds for 1 MB on a phone. The cost needs a device profile to quantify.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:621`

## Problem
SendTextAsync encodes the string (:22-43), SendMessageAsync takes the uncontended locks synchronously (:611), WriteMessageWithExtensionsAsync runs TransformOutbound (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:30: full-message deflate, on Mono possibly the managed SyncFlushDeflater), and the frame writer copies and masks the first chunk, all before the first await that can yield. None of it is offloaded.

**Failure scenario.** SendAsync of a large message from the Unity main thread with compression enabled compresses and masks the payload inside that frame (plausibly tens of milliseconds for 1 MB on a phone) before the call returns its Task. Needs a device profile to quantify.

## Suggested fix
Above a size threshold run the transform on the thread pool before taking the frame lock, or document that large sends must not be issued from the main thread.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Above a documented size threshold the transform runs off the calling thread before the frame lock is taken, or the documentation states that large sends must not be issued from the main thread
- [ ] The measured main-thread time of SendAsync for a 1 MB compressed message is recorded on a device and validated

title: [WebSocket] A data write stalled by TCP backpressure holds the frame lock with no deadline and starves keep-alive pings, Pongs and protocol-error Close
body:
## Summary
WriteFrameLockedAsync holds _sendLock across the socket write with only the caller's token, and options have no send timeout. The keep-alive Ping waits for the same lock, so a stalled write prevents PongTimeout from ever firing, and Pong replies and the protocol-error Close are blocked as well. On a network that goes dark without RST the connection stays Open for minutes.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:728`

## Problem
Every frame goes through WriteFrameLockedAsync, which holds _sendLock across frame.WriteAsync(writer, stream, ct) (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:728-760) with only the caller's token; WebSocketConnectionOptions has no send or write timeout. The keep-alive loop sends its Ping through the same funnel with the keep-alive token and no timeout (972-979), so while a data write is blocked it waits at _sendLock.WaitAsync and never reaches WaitForPongAfterAsync (1000) or the IdleTimeout check of the next iteration (945). The receive loop answers a peer Ping inline through the same lock (389-394), and TryHandleProtocolErrorAsync sends its Close with the lifecycle token and no timeout (519), unlike the Close reply (444-446) and CloseCoreAsync (136-137), which are bounded by CloseHandshakeTimeout.

**Failure scenario.** A mobile network goes dark without a RST (platform.md: no SO_KEEPALIVE) while the app sends a message larger than the free socket send buffer with ct = default. The write blocks; PingInterval/PongTimeout (25 s + 10 s) cannot fire because the Ping cannot take the frame lock, so the connection stays Open until the OS retransmission timeout fails the write (minutes). If the peer sends a Ping meanwhile, the receive loop blocks on the Pong and inbound delivery stops too.

## Suggested fix
Bound how long a frame write may hold the frame lock (a send timeout that aborts the connection the way #79 does for cancellation), or let the keep-alive loop treat a Ping that cannot be written within PongTimeout as a dead peer and call FinalizeClose (disposing the stream faults the stalled write). Bound the protocol-error Close with CloseHandshakeTimeout.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A frame write that holds the frame lock longer than a bounded timeout aborts the connection (or the keep-alive treats an unwritable Ping within PongTimeout as a dead peer and finalizes)
- [ ] The protocol-error Close is bounded by CloseHandshakeTimeout
- [ ] The new timeout is an option with documented default and XML docs
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix and passes after it using a stalled stream

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-protocol-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described. WriteFrameLockedAsync holds _sendLock across frame.WriteAsync with only the caller token (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:728-760); WebSocketConnectionOptions has no send/write timeout and no socket send timeout is set anywhere in Runtime/WebSocket or Runtime/WebSocket.Transport. The keep-alive Ping goes through the same funnel (:972-979) and reaches WaitForPongAfterAsync (:1000) only after the write returns, so a stalled data write (or the Ping write itself when the socket send buffer is already full) leaves the loop parked with no deadline. The Pong reply to a peer Ping (:389-394) and the protocol-error Close (:519, lifecycle token only, also waits for _messageLock at :585) are unbounded too, unlike the Close reply (:444-446) and CloseCoreAsync (:136-137). Precondition I checked: pings are not suppressed by outbound activity (dueIn is computed once per iteration, :929-932), so the stall needs the send buffer to fill before a Ping is written and its PongTimeout fires, i.e. the app sends more than the free send buffer within about PingInterval+PongTimeout of the network going dark. Realistic for uploads/bursty senders on mobile; then the connection stays Open until the OS gives up on retransmission. No tracking issue (#162 is the HTTP header-phase reads).

Also reported as `ws-runtime-08` (merged into this issue).

title: [WebSocket] Keep-alive publishes _lastPingTimestamp after the ping write so a fast pong is measured against the previous ping
body:
## Summary
The keep-alive loop stores the ping timestamp only after the write and the metrics callback. If the pong is handled before that store, the RTT is computed against the previous ping, about PingInterval, which skews the health monitor and can report Critical quality on a healthy link.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:998`

## Problem
The keep-alive loop takes pingTimestamp before the write (:961) but stores it in _lastPingTimestamp only at :998, after the write completed and after RecordFrameSent/RecordPingSent/TryPublishMetricsUpdate (:981-983), which can run a user MetricsUpdated handler (on an idle connection every ping exceeds the 5 s MetricsUpdateInterval). The pong handler computes the RTT from _lastPingTimestamp (:414-421).

**Failure scenario.** If the pong is processed before :998 runs (loopback or LAN RTT shorter than the metrics handler), the RTT sample is taken against the previous ping, about PingInterval (25 s): the health monitor's average jumps and ConnectionQualityChanged reports Critical on a healthy link. Needs a low-latency link and a subscribed metrics handler to observe.

## Suggested fix
Store _lastPingTimestamp before writing the ping and match the RTT to the echoed ping counter.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] _lastPingTimestamp is stored before the ping is written
- [ ] The RTT sample is matched to the echoed ping counter
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix and passes after it with a pong that arrives before the metrics callback returns

title: [WebSocket] Keep-alive counts only complete Pong frames as liveness so a large inbound frame in transit aborts a healthy connection
body:
## Summary
WaitForPongAfterAsync only looks at the timestamp of a fully read Pong, and the frame reader returns only after a whole frame (up to 4 MB) is read. A Pong cannot be interleaved inside a frame, so a Ping sent during a slow large transfer times out and the connection is closed with PongTimeout in the middle of the message.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:1000`

## Problem
After a Ping, WaitForPongAfterAsync (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:1033-1066) looks only at _lastPongTimestamp, which is set once a Pong frame has been read completely (401-411). The only forgiveness is ReceiveLoopParkedSince (1004, local backpressure, #78). WebSocketFrameReader.ReadAsync reads a whole frame, up to MaxFrameSize (4 MB), before it returns (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:234-240) and exposes no progress; a server cannot interleave a Pong inside a frame (RFC 6455 5.4), so the Pong sits behind the remaining payload. TouchActivity is also called only for complete control frames and messages (248, 310).

**Failure scenario.** Idle connection with the default PingInterval 25 s and PongTimeout 10 s. The server starts a 2 MB frame over a 100 KB/s mobile link (20 s). A Ping fired during the transfer gets its Pong only after the frame ends; when more than 10 s of payload remain, the loop calls FinalizeClose(AbnormalClosure, PongTimeout) (1011-1016) in the middle of the message. The same happens on a slow uplink where the Ping queues behind buffered outbound data.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 5.5.2

## Suggested fix
Treat bytes read from the socket as liveness: let the frame reader stamp a last-bytes-received timestamp per read and have the Pong wait forgive or extend while that timestamp advanced after the Ping. Confirm with a peer that sends one large frame through a throttled stream.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bytes received from the socket count as liveness: the Pong wait is extended while data arrived after the Ping
- [ ] A connection receiving a large frame over a throttled stream is not closed with PongTimeout while bytes keep arriving
- [ ] A silent peer is still closed after PongTimeout
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WaitForPongAfterAsync looks only at _lastPongTimestamp (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:1038-1060), set when a complete Pong frame has been read (:401-411). The only forgiveness is ReceiveLoopParkedSince (:1004, local backpressure). WebSocketFrameReader.ReadAsync returns only after the whole payload, up to MaxFrameSize 4 MB, was read (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:234-240) and exposes no progress; TouchActivity runs only for complete control frames (:248) and complete messages (:310), not even for non-final fragments (:252-253). A Pong cannot be interleaved inside a frame (RFC 6455 5.4), so a Ping sent while more than PongTimeout (10 s) of an inbound frame remains ends in FinalizeClose(AbnormalClosure, PongTimeout) (:1011-1016) on a healthy connection. Needs a single frame (or server-queued data ahead of the Pong) that takes more than 10 s to arrive, e.g. 1-2 MB on a slow mobile link, and a Ping falling in that window; edge case but deterministic once the timing is met. No test covers a throttled large frame with keep-alive on.

title: [WebSocket] Keep-alive deadlines run across application suspension with no resume handling and can close a live connection
body:
## Summary
Keep-alive uses Task.Delay and CancelAfter and nothing observes application pause or resume. If the app is suspended after a Ping and the Pong arrives while frozen, the expired timer can win over the receive completion on resume and close a live connection with PongTimeout.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:1000`

## Problem
The keep-alive deadlines are a Task.Delay (:932) and a CancelAfter inside WaitForPongAfterAsync (:1050-1051); nothing observes application pause or resume, and the only forgiveness after a timeout is local backpressure (:1004-1009).

**Failure scenario.** The app is suspended (iOS/Android backgrounding) right after a ping was written; the pong reaches the kernel while the process is frozen. On resume the pong timer has already expired and can be dispatched before the receive loop's read completion: FinalizeClose(PongTimeout) on a connection that is still alive, which a plain WebSocketClient does not reconnect. Device-only: needs a suspend/resume run on iOS and Android to confirm the ordering.

## Suggested fix
On a pong timeout re-check _lastPongTimestamp after giving the receive loop a bounded grace period before declaring the peer dead, and let the Unity layer signal resume so the keep-alive restarts its deadline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On pong timeout _lastPongTimestamp is re-checked after a bounded grace period before declaring the peer dead
- [ ] The Unity layer can signal resume so the keep-alive restarts its deadline
- [ ] Suspend/resume ordering validated on iOS and Android and recorded on a device
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix and passes after it for the grace-period logic

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketConnection is a 2,350-line multi-responsibility class with duplicated fragmentation rules and unowned shared fields
body:
## Summary
WebSocketConnection is split into four partial files that share about 35 mutable fields and do not follow responsibilities. The outbound fragmentation rule exists in three places and frame-header length rules in two, so metrics can disagree with sent frames, and close-status fields lack a single owner.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:13`

## Problem
The four partial files (417 + 1068 + 585 + 281 lines) share about 35 mutable fields and hold the handshake orchestration, the state machine, both send locks, the receive loop, control-frame handling, the close handshake, the keep-alive loop, the extension pipeline, metrics/health publishing, wire-size arithmetic and a nested 150-line Stream wrapper; the split does not follow responsibilities (the keep-alive loop is in SendReceive.cs:923-1066, PrefetchedStream, wire-length maths and stopwatch helpers in Lifecycle.cs:277-583). Consequences visible in the code: the outbound fragmentation rule is written three times (WriteMessageFramesAsync, SendReceive.cs:673-704; CalculateMessageWireStats, Lifecycle.cs:277-303, which re-derives sizes for metrics instead of the writer reporting them; and WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteMessageAsync, WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:213-238, which the connection never calls), and frame-header length rules twice (CalculateFrameWireLength vs BuildHeader). `_hasCloseStatus`/`_closeStatus` are plain fields written by the receive loop (flag first, then the two-word struct, SendReceive.cs:432-433) and by FinalizeClose on any thread (Lifecycle.cs:104-105) and read by senders/receivers (SendReceive.cs:93-94, 843-844); `_healthMonitor` is read twice around a call (SendReceive.cs:415-420) while FinalizeClose nulls it (Lifecycle.cs:159-163).

**Failure scenario.** A change to fragmentation (for example per-fragment RSV handling or a different threshold rule) applied in one of the three copies makes sent frames and reported BytesSent/FramesSent disagree; a sender racing the receive loop's Close handling can build a WebSocketException with CloseCode 0 because the flag is visible before the struct; the review history (#78-#86, #208, #217, #301, #320, #375) shows most defects came from interactions across these partials.

## Suggested fix
Extract cohesive collaborators with explicit ownership: a send pipeline (locks, fragmentation, wire accounting returned by the writer), a keep-alive monitor, a close coordinator holding the close status behind one volatile reference, and move PrefetchedStream to its own file; delete the unused writer-level fragmentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Send pipeline, keep-alive monitor and close coordinator are extracted as collaborators with explicit field ownership
- [ ] Fragmentation and frame wire-size rules live in one place and the writer reports the wire stats used by metrics
- [ ] Close status is held behind one volatile reference
- [ ] Existing WebSocket tests in Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ pass unchanged and a regression test covers metrics matching the sent frames

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-14` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The facts hold; the failure scenarios are mostly hypothetical, so this is a maintainability item. Verified: the four partials are 417 + 1068 + 585 + 281 lines; the keep-alive loop sits in SendReceive.cs:923-1066 and PrefetchedStream, wire-length maths and stopwatch helpers in Lifecycle.cs:277-583. The fragmentation rule exists three times: WriteMessageFramesAsync (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:673-704), CalculateMessageWireStats (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:277-303, called after the write at Extensions.cs:58-64) and WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteMessageAsync (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:194-238), which no runtime code calls (the connection only uses WriteFrameAsync and WriteCloseAsync, SendReceive.cs:889-895, WebSocketConnection.cs:389); header length is derived twice (Lifecycle.cs:305-320 vs WebSocketFrameWriter.BuildHeader :361). Concurrency: _hasCloseStatus/_closeStatus/_terminalError are plain fields (WebSocketConnection.cs:66-68) written by the receive loop, flag before the two-word struct (SendReceive.cs:432-433), and by FinalizeClose on any thread (Lifecycle.cs:104-105), and read without Volatile by ReceiveAsync, CreateClosedException and the CloseStatus property (SendReceive.cs:93-94, :843-844; WebSocketConnection.cs:142). That breaks the CLAUDE.md section 4 'one owner' rule, but the observable outcome (CloseCode 0 or a mismatched reason) needs a second thread's FinalizeClose (Abort, pong timeout) to land between the two receive-loop stores while a third thread reads, because readers only reach those paths after FinalizeClose published Closed through Interlocked (Lifecycle.cs:122-151). The _healthMonitor double read (SendReceive.cs:415-420 vs Lifecycle.cs:159-163) can at worst throw a NullReferenceException that the receive loop's catch-all swallows into an already-finalized FinalizeClose (SendReceive.cs:370-376). #182 tracks oversized files in Core only, so no open issue covers this.

title: [WebSocket] Dead members in shipping code: unread _lastPongCounter, unused writer and metrics members, duplicated IsHeaderToken
body:
## Summary
Several members have no reader or caller: _lastPongCounter (so pong payloads are never verified), the writer's fragmentation threshold and mask lock, RecordFramesReceived, handshake result/request properties and an unreachable assembler branch. IsHeaderToken is duplicated in three places and PerMessageDeflateExtension has three identical catch bodies. Unused public members become API commitments at 1.0.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:84`

## Problem
`_lastPongCounter` is written on every 8-byte pong and never read (WebSocketConnection.cs:84; SendReceive.cs:405-409), so the ping counter payload is never matched and any pong satisfies the waiter by timestamp. WebSocketFrameWriter keeps `_fragmentationThreshold` and a `_maskKeyLock` (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:22, 27) that serve only the unused WriteMessageAsync path and a class documented as not thread-safe. WebSocketMetricsCollector.RecordFramesReceived has no caller (WebSocketMetricsCollector.cs:74). WebSocketHandshakeResult.NegotiatedExtensions (a comma split that ignores quoted parameters, WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:250), ErrorBodyText and ThrowIfFailed, WebSocketHandshakeRequest.RequestedExtensions/HostHeader/RequestTarget and WebSocketFrame.IsDataFrame have no runtime reader. MessageAssembler.TryAssemble has a control-frame branch (MessageAssembler.cs:62-66) the connection never reaches because it handles control frames before the assembler (SendReceive.cs:238-250). PerMessageDeflateExtension.TransformInbound has three catch clauses with identical bodies (PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:216-236). IsHeaderToken is duplicated verbatim in WebSocketHandshake.cs:307-342 and WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:305-340, with a third token table in IWebSocketExtension.cs:133-161.

**Failure scenario.** A maintainer assumes pong payloads are verified because the counter is stored, or fixes token validation in one of the three copies; unused public members become API commitments at 1.0.

## Suggested fix
Delete the unread field or actually compare the echoed counter, remove the unused writer/collector/handshake members (or make them internal test helpers), and keep one token validator.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unread fields and unused members are removed or made internal test helpers; the pong counter is either compared or deleted
- [ ] One header-token validator is shared by the handshake, options and extension code
- [ ] Identical catch clauses in PerMessageDeflateExtension.TransformInbound are merged
- [ ] Existing tests in Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ pass and the shadow build shows no new analyzer warning

title: [WebSocket] Abort or Dispose during WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync neither cancels the transport connect nor disposes the stream that arrives afterwards
body:
## Summary
The handshake token is linked only to the caller's token, not _lifecycleCts. Abort or Dispose during transport.ConnectAsync finalizes while _stream is still null, so the stream returned later is never disposed, the server sees a completed upgrade and the socket stays open until GC. This also applies to injected transports, which WebSocketClient does not dispose.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:193`

## Problem
ConnectAsync links the handshake token to the caller's ct only (:188-191); _lifecycleCts (:175) is not linked. Abort()/Dispose() during 'await transport.ConnectAsync' (:193) run FinalizeClose, which disposes Interlocked.Exchange(ref _stream, null) (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:156) while _stream is still null. When the transport returns, :193 stores the stream, the upgrade request is sent and validated, and TryTransitionState(Connecting, Open) fails at :292 because the state is Closed; the catch at :322-365 calls FinalizeClose again, a no-op (Lifecycle.cs:101), so the stream is never disposed. RawSocketWebSocketTransport only notices disposal of the transport itself (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:188, :237), which WebSocketClient does for an owned transport on Dispose() but not on Abort() (WebSocketClient.cs:330-334) and never for a caller-provided transport (:668-676).

**Failure scenario.** client.Abort() (or Dispose() with an injected transport, or WebSocketConnection.Dispose()) while ConnectAsync is still resolving or connecting: the connect is not cancelled, the server sees a completed WebSocket upgrade, ConnectAsync then throws 'Failed to transition connection from Connecting to Open', and the connected socket or TLS stream stays open until the GC finalizes it.

## Suggested fix
Link _lifecycleCts.Token into handshakeCts so Abort/Dispose cancel the connect, and after transport.ConnectAsync returns (and in the catch blocks) dispose the stream when the connection is already finalized.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Abort/Dispose during ConnectAsync cancels the transport connect via _lifecycleCts linked into the handshake token
- [ ] A stream returned after the connection was finalized is disposed in the success path and in the catch blocks
- [ ] ConnectAsync throws a cancellation or closed error instead of an invalid state transition message
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ that fails before the fix and passes after it with a transport that completes after Abort

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: resource-management.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. handshakeCts links only the caller's ct (WebSocketConnection.cs:188-189); _lifecycleCts (:175) is not linked. Abort during 'await transport.ConnectAsync' (:193) reaches FinalizeClose via AbortCore (Lifecycle.cs:64-69) while _stream is null, so :156 disposes nothing. When the transport returns, :193 stores the stream, the upgrade is written and validated (:216-222), TryTransitionState(Connecting, Open) fails at :292 because the state is Closed, and the catch at :322-365 calls FinalizeClose again, a no-op (Lifecycle.cs:101). WebSocketClient's cleanup then calls connection.DisposeAsync, which returns at AbortCore's Closed check (Lifecycle.cs:64-65), and disposes an owned transport, but RawSocketWebSocketTransport.Dispose only sets a flag (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:281-284) that is checked before the stream is handed out (:188, :237), never afterwards. The stream and socket stay open until GC. WebSocketClient.Abort does not dispose the transport (WebSocketClient.cs:330-334), so the window is the whole DNS+TCP+TLS phase; for Dispose with an owned transport the :188/:237 checks close most of it, for an injected transport nothing does. No test aborts during connect (WebSocketConnectCancellationTests covers token cancel and timeout only).

title: [WebSocket] Metrics collection is always on per connection and cannot be disabled or stripped
body:
## Summary
WebSocketConnection creates a WebSocketMetricsCollector unconditionally, while the health monitor is behind EnableHealthMonitoring. Each received and sent message takes the collector lock three times and reads the clock four to five times for counters the application may never read. Both collector and health monitor are statically referenced, so they link into every build that uses a WebSocket.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:272`

## Problem
`_metrics = new WebSocketMetricsCollector();` is unconditional (WebSocketConnection.cs:272) while the health monitor is behind EnableHealthMonitoring (:273-275). Setting MetricsUpdateMessageInterval and MetricsUpdateInterval to zero only stops the events (WebSocketMetricsCollector.cs:147-163). Per received data message the receive loop takes the collector lock three times (RecordFrameReceived, RecordMessageReceived, ShouldPublishSnapshot; SendReceive.cs:236, 308-309) with a Stopwatch read in each, plus TouchActivity's Stopwatch read, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow and three Interlocked writes (Lifecycle.cs:331-341); the send path does the same. WebSocketMetricsCollector (210 lines) and WebSocketHealthMonitor (231 lines) are statically referenced from WebSocketConnection, so both are linked into every build that uses a WebSocket.

**Failure scenario.** A high-rate stream (thousands of small frames per second on a mobile CPU) pays three uncontended lock round trips and four to five clock reads per message for counters the application never reads, and there is no switch to remove the cost or the code.

## Suggested fix
Add an EnableMetrics option (null collector when off, as for the health monitor), fold the three per-message collector calls into one, and reference the health monitor only from an opt-in path so it strips when unused.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WebSocketConnectionOptions has an EnableMetrics option; when off, no collector is allocated and the per-message path takes no collector lock or extra clock read
- [ ] With metrics on, the per-message collector calls are folded into one lock acquisition per message
- [ ] The health monitor is referenced only from an opt-in path so it can be stripped when unused

title: [WebSocket] IdleTimeout is only evaluated in the keep-alive loop, so it is ignored when PingInterval is zero
body:
## Summary
The keep-alive task starts only when PingInterval is greater than zero, and it is the sole reader of IdleTimeout. Validate accepts PingInterval = 0 with IdleTimeout > 0, so that combination never times out. With keep-alive on, the check runs once per wake-up and aborts with AbnormalClosure without a Close frame. The option is untested and undocumented.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:300`

## Problem
The keep-alive task is started only `if (_options.PingInterval > TimeSpan.Zero)` (WebSocketConnection.cs:300-304) and the sole IdleTimeout check is inside RunKeepAliveLoopAsync (SendReceive.cs:945-958). Validate accepts PingInterval = 0 with IdleTimeout > 0 (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:223-232). With keep-alive on, the check runs once per wake-up, so its resolution is PingInterval plus PongTimeout, and it aborts with AbnormalClosure without sending a Close frame. No test sets a non-zero IdleTimeout and the option is not in Documentation~.

**Failure scenario.** `new WebSocketConnectionOptions { PingInterval = TimeSpan.Zero, IdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2) }` (server-driven pings, client-side idle cut-off): the connection stays open indefinitely with no traffic; UnityWebSocketClient with ping interval 0 behaves the same.

## Suggested fix
Run the idle check from its own timer independent of pings (or reject the combination in Validate), close with a Close frame (1001) rather than an abort, and add a test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] IdleTimeout is enforced independent of PingInterval (own timer), or the combination PingInterval = 0 with IdleTimeout > 0 is rejected by Validate
- [ ] An idle timeout closes the connection with a Close frame (1001) before falling back to abort
- [ ] IdleTimeout is documented in Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md

title: [WebSocket] ConnectAsync reads _lifecycleCts after the connection is Open, so a concurrent finalization fails connect with NullReferenceException
body:
## Summary
After the Connecting-to-Open transition, ConnectAsync re-reads _lifecycleCts without synchronisation to start the receive loop and to link the keep-alive CTS. FinalizeClose can run on another thread (Abort/Dispose) or inside the receive loop and sets that field to null and disposes it. The connect then fails with a NullReferenceException or ObjectDisposedException message, and a keep-alive CTS created afterwards is never disposed.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:302`

## Problem
After the Connecting->Open transition (:292) ConnectAsync reads _lifecycleCts without synchronisation at :298 (to start the receive loop) and :302 (to link the keep-alive CTS). From :292 on, FinalizeClose can run on another thread (Abort/Dispose) or inside ReceiveLoopAsync itself when the first read and the close path complete synchronously; it exchanges _lifecycleCts with null and may dispose it (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:117, :213-229). A keep-alive CTS created at :302 after that pass is never cancelled or disposed.

**Failure scenario.** Abort()/Dispose() from another thread just as the handshake completes, or a server Close frame processed synchronously with the 101 (in-memory transports): '_lifecycleCts.Token' throws, and ConnectAsync fails with WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed, 'Object reference not set...') instead of returning a connection that reports its close status.

## Suggested fix
Capture the lifecycle CTS and token in a local before the state transition and use only the local; create and store the keep-alive CTS before starting the receive loop, or re-check finalization after storing it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectAsync captures the lifecycle CTS and token in a local before the state transition and uses only the local
- [ ] The keep-alive CTS is created and stored before the receive loop starts, or finalization is re-checked after storing it, so it is always disposed
- [ ] Abort/Dispose racing the handshake completion yields a connection reporting its close status, not a WebSocketException with a null-reference message

title: [WebSocket] Connect timeouts, DNS, TLS certificate and protocol failures all surface as ConnectionClosed/NetworkError and are retryable
body:
## Summary
WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync maps every non-WebSocketException and the handshake timeout to WebSocketError.ConnectionClosed, which maps to UHttpErrorType.NetworkError. TLS certificate failures, DNS timeouts and usage errors therefore look like retryable network drops, unlike the HTTP client that reports CertificateError and Timeout. On the receive side every WebSocketProtocolException is rewrapped as ProtocolViolation, and several public enum members are never observable.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnection.cs:354`

## Problem
WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync maps every non-WebSocketException to `new WebSocketException(WebSocketError.ConnectionClosed, ex.Message, ex)` (WebSocketConnection.cs:352-355) and the handshake timeout to ConnectionClosed too (338-347); WebSocketException.MapErrorType turns ConnectionClosed into UHttpErrorType.NetworkError (WebSocketException.cs:127-133). The transport lets the TLS provider's AuthenticationException, the DNS TimeoutException (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:343) and its own ArgumentException for a non-ws scheme (:386-390) propagate, so all of them arrive as ConnectionClosed/NetworkError with IsRetryable() == true. The HTTP transport maps the same faults to UHttpErrorType.CertificateError (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:821) and UHttpErrorType.Timeout; WebSocketError has no Timeout or Certificate member and UHttpErrorType.Timeout/CertificateError are never produced in this module. On the receive side TryHandleProtocolErrorAsync rewraps every WebSocketProtocolException as WebSocketError.ProtocolViolation (SendReceive.cs:508-512), so InvalidFrame, FrameTooLarge, InvalidUtf8, MaskedServerFrame, UnexpectedContinuation, ReservedOpcode, PayloadLengthOverflow and MessageTooLarge are never observable on WebSocketException.Error although they are public enum members listed in IsRetryable. Server-side faults map to UHttpErrorType.InvalidRequest (WebSocketException.cs:108-125), a handshake rejection carries no UHttpError.StatusCode (only HandshakeStatusCode), FrameTooLarge falls to Unknown, and ProxyTunnelFailed is NetworkError (HttpError.IsRetryable() true) but WebSocketException.IsRetryable() false. ResilientWebSocketClient uses neither definition (IsPermanentConnectFailure, :639-652).

**Failure scenario.** The server certificate expires while a ResilientWebSocketClient with WebSocketReconnectPolicy.Infinite is connected: every reconnect fails TLS validation, surfaces as ConnectionClosed/NetworkError and is retried forever; the app cannot tell a certificate failure or a handshake timeout from a dropped connection except by inspecting InnerException. Code switching on `ex.Error == WebSocketError.MessageTooLarge` never matches.

## Suggested fix
Map connect failures by cause at one place (timeout -> a Timeout error and UHttpErrorType.Timeout, AuthenticationException -> a certificate error, ArgumentException -> rethrow as usage error), keep the specific WebSocketError of a protocol exception when rewrapping, pass the handshake status into UHttpError, and derive one retryability rule that the resilient client also uses (certificate and usage errors permanent).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TLS certificate failures surface as UHttpErrorType.CertificateError and are not retried by ResilientWebSocketClient; connect and handshake timeouts surface as UHttpErrorType.Timeout
- [ ] DNS and usage errors (for example a non-ws scheme) are distinguished from dropped connections; handshake rejection carries the HTTP status in UHttpError.StatusCode
- [ ] WebSocketError exposes the specific protocol error values the receive path produces, and IsRetryable is consistent with the HTTP error model including ProxyTunnelFailed
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ connects to a server with an untrusted certificate and to an unresponsive handshake and asserts the error type and IsRetryable and fails before the fix

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync maps the handshake timeout to ConnectionClosed (WebSocketConnection.cs:338-347) and every other non-WebSocketException to ConnectionClosed (:352-355); ConnectionClosed -> UHttpErrorType.NetworkError and IsRetryable() true (WebSocketException.cs:66-73, 127-133). The transport lets TimeoutException (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:343), the TLS provider's AuthenticationException (WrapAsync :230, rethrown :245-249) and ArgumentException for a bad scheme (:386-390, called inside the connection's try at WebSocketConnection.cs:191) propagate. The HTTP transport maps AuthenticationException to CertificateError (RawSocketTransport.cs:819-821). TryHandleProtocolErrorAsync rewraps every WebSocketProtocolException as ProtocolViolation (SendReceive.cs:508-512), the specific code survives only as InnerException (tests asserting MessageTooLarge/MaskedServerFrame do so on the reader/assembler directly, WebSocketMessageLimitTests.cs:27-31, WebSocketFramingTests.cs:199-204). IsPermanentConnectFailure handles only ProxyAuthenticationRequired and 4xx handshakes (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:639-652), so a certificate failure is retried for as long as the policy allows. No certificate is accepted that should not be; this is error classification, not a TLS weakening.
