title: [WebSocket] TlsProvider is an untyped object on WebSocketConnectionOptions and cleartext policy is enforced only in the built-in transport
body:
## Summary
WebSocketConnectionOptions carries transport settings (TlsProvider as object, DnsTimeoutMs, ProxySettings, AllowCleartext) that only RawSocketWebSocketTransport reads. A wrong-typed TlsProvider compiles and fails at connect as a retryable ConnectionClosed. A custom IWebSocketTransport bypasses the cleartext and proxy-credential policy, and options are cloned and re-validated three to five times per connect.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:111`

## Problem
`public object TlsProvider` (:111) documents that the runtime type must be TurboHTTP.Transport.Tls.ITlsProvider, which the WebSocket assembly cannot name; RawSocketWebSocketTransport casts it and throws ArgumentException otherwise (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:286-296), and WebSocketConnection wraps that as WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed) (WebSocketConnection.cs:354). DnsTimeoutMs (an int in milliseconds next to TimeSpan timeouts), ConnectTimeout, ProxySettings, TlsBackend, TlsProvider and AllowCleartext are all read only by RawSocketWebSocketTransport (:84-123, :97-111); IWebSocketTransport.ConnectAsync receives the whole options object (IWebSocketTransport.cs:14-17) with no statement of which members an implementation must honour. The cleartext and proxy-credential policy checks therefore do not run for any other IWebSocketTransport. Each layer also re-clones and re-validates the options (WebSocketClient.cs:109, WebSocketConnection.cs:167, RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:69, ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:102 and 346): three to five deep copies including HttpHeaders per connect.

**Failure scenario.** A project sets `options.TlsProvider = myPinningCallback` (wrong type): it compiles and fails at connect with a retryable 'ConnectionClosed' network error. A project plugs in its own IWebSocketTransport (for example a tunnelling or test transport) and ws:// connections proceed on iOS/Android although AllowCleartext is false, because nothing above the transport checks it.

## Suggested fix
Move TLS provider, DNS/connect timeouts and Happy Eyeballs settings to a typed transport options object owned by TurboHTTP.WebSocket.Transport (constructor or factory argument), keep protocol settings on WebSocketConnectionOptions, and enforce CleartextTrafficPolicy in WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync before calling any transport. Clone once at the public entry point and pass the frozen copy down.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TLS provider and transport timeouts move to a typed transport options object owned by the WebSocket transport assembly; WebSocketConnectionOptions keeps protocol settings only
- [ ] CleartextTrafficPolicy is enforced in WebSocketConnection.ConnectAsync before any transport is called
- [ ] Options are cloned and validated once at the public entry point
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ plugs in a custom IWebSocketTransport and asserts ws:// is rejected when AllowCleartext is false and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described, but the impact is API shape, not a defect in a default path. Verified: `public object TlsProvider` (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:111); RawSocketWebSocketTransport.ResolveTlsProvider casts it and throws ArgumentException (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:286-296), which WebSocketConnection maps to WebSocketException(ConnectionClosed) (WebSocketConnection.cs:352-355), an error IsRetryable() reports true for (WebSocketException.cs:75). DnsTimeoutMs, ConnectTimeout, ProxySettings, TlsProvider and AllowCleartext are read only in RawSocketWebSocketTransport (:84-123, :199, :288); TlsBackend is also read at WebSocketClient.cs:174 to pick the default transport (small inaccuracy). IWebSocketTransport.ConnectAsync takes the whole options object with no contract (IWebSocketTransport.cs:14-17). Clones: WebSocketClient.cs:109 + WebSocketConnection.cs:167 + RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:69 = 3 per plain connect, plus ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:102 and :346 = 5 on a resilient first connect; connect-time only, negligible cost. Weakened part: the cleartext check living in the transport is the documented design, not an oversight: CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:12-15 says the HTTP transport and the WebSocket transport apply the policy, the HTTP side does the same (RawSocketTransport.cs:487-495), and the policy class is public for custom transports. Only the AllowCleartext doc (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:117-126, 'the connect throws ... before any socket is opened') overstates it for a custom IWebSocketTransport; note WebSocketConnection already hosts one transport-independent pre-check (WireHost, WebSocketConnection.cs:182-186). Adjacent defect found while tracing (not in the finding): ResolveTlsProvider is called outside the try (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:225, try starts :227) and ConnectAsync disposes the stream only on cancellation (:156-160), so a wrong-typed TlsProvider, or TlsBackend.BouncyCastle without the opt-in define (TlsProviderSelector.cs:85-95 throws InvalidOperationException), leaves the connected socket (and CONNECT tunnel) undisposed on every wss:// attempt until finalization.

title: [WebSocket] WithCompression captures MaxMessageSize at call time so the decompression limit diverges from the connection limit
body:
## Summary
WithCompression copies MaxMessageSize into a closure when called, and the permessage-deflate extension enforces that stale value while the connection uses the current one. Setting MaxMessageSize after WithCompression makes the extension reject messages the connection allows, or inflate up to the stale limit when the limit was lowered, weakening the decompression bound. Clones keep the stale closure.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:164`

## Problem
`int maxMessageSize = MaxMessageSize; return WithExtension(() => new PerMessageDeflateExtension(effectiveOptions, maxMessageSize));` (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:163-165). The factory runs later (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:190-213) with the captured value; PerMessageDeflateExtension.Decompress throws DecompressedMessageTooLarge above it (PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:353-359), which the receive loop turns into a protocol failure that closes the connection (SendReceive.cs:334-345). The connection's own check uses the current `_options.MaxMessageSize` (Extensions.cs:132). IWebSocketExtension factories receive no context, so there is no other way for an extension to learn the limit. The only test builds options in the safe order (WebSocketExtensionTests.cs:182-184).

**Failure scenario.** `var o = new WebSocketConnectionOptions().WithCompression(); o.MaxMessageSize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;` (fluent call first, then tuning): a 6 MB compressed message that is within the configured limit is rejected by the extension at the stale 4 MB default and the connection is closed. In the other direction (limit lowered afterwards) the extension inflates up to 4 MB before the connection rejects the message, weakening the configured bound.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the limit when the connection creates the extension: pass a small context (MaxMessageSize at least) to the factory (`Func<WebSocketExtensionContext, IWebSocketExtension>`) or to TransformInbound, and have WithCompression read it from there.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The extension factory or TransformInbound receives the connection's effective MaxMessageSize at connect time and WithCompression no longer captures it
- [ ] Raising or lowering MaxMessageSize after WithCompression changes the decompression limit accordingly
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ calls WithCompression before and after setting MaxMessageSize and asserts the effective decompression limit equals the final MaxMessageSize and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-12` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WithCompression copies MaxMessageSize into a local and closes over it (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:163-165); the factory runs at connect (WebSocketConnection.cs:202 -> WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:190-213) and PerMessageDeflateExtension keeps the value as readonly _maxMessageSize (PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:26, :51) and enforces it in Decompress (:353-358). Clone copies the factory list (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:190-192), so the stale closure survives every clone. With `new WebSocketConnectionOptions().WithCompression(); o.MaxMessageSize = 16 MB` Validate passes (MaxFrameSize 4 MB <= 16 MB <= 4 MB * 64), the frame reader/assembler use 16 MB (WebSocketConnection.cs:173, :279-282), and a message inflating past 4 MB throws DecompressedMessageTooLarge, which the receive loop turns into a protocol failure and closes the connection (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:334-345; the close code is 1002, not 1009). Lowering the limit afterwards lets the extension inflate up to the captured value into a MemoryStream before the connection-level check rejects it (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:132-137). No guard: IWebSocketExtension factories take no arguments, and the documented snippet is the fluent form that invites setting properties afterwards (Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:169-170). Tests only use the safe order (WebSocketExtensionTests.cs:182-184; WebSocketMessageLimitTests.cs:271-277 sets the limit without compression). An object initializer followed by .WithCompression() is safe, so this is order-dependent, hence medium.

Also reported as `ws-protocol-13` (merged into this issue).

title: [WebSocket] TimeSpan options above int.MaxValue ms pass Validate and then throw in CancelAfter or Task.Delay
body:
## Summary
Validate checks only the sign of CloseHandshakeTimeout, HandshakeTimeout, PingInterval and PongTimeout. Values above about 24.8 days (such as TimeSpan.MaxValue) make CancelAfter and Task.Delay throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException. The keep-alive loop reports that as a pong timeout, and CloseAsync throws after moving to Closing without sending a Close frame. The same applies to WebSocketReconnectPolicy.MaxDelay.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:223`

## Problem
Validate checks only the sign of CloseHandshakeTimeout, HandshakeTimeout, PingInterval and PongTimeout (:219-226). They feed CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter (WebSocketConnection.cs:189; WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:137, :446, :542, :1051) and Task.Delay (:932, :941), which throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException above int.MaxValue milliseconds (about 24.8 days). The same holds for WebSocketReconnectPolicy.MaxDelay (ResilientWebSocketClient.cs:574).

**Failure scenario.** PongTimeout or PingInterval = TimeSpan.MaxValue (a common spelling of 'no timeout'): the keep-alive loop throws and its catch-all finalizes the connection as AbnormalClosure with a PongTimeout error (SendReceive.cs:1024-1029). CloseHandshakeTimeout = TimeSpan.MaxValue makes CloseAsync throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException after the state already moved to Closing (:133-137), with no Close frame sent.

## Suggested fix
Reject (or clamp, or treat as infinite) values above int.MaxValue milliseconds in Validate for every TimeSpan that feeds CancelAfter or Task.Delay.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Validate rejects, clamps or treats as infinite every TimeSpan above int.MaxValue milliseconds that feeds CancelAfter or Task.Delay, including WebSocketReconnectPolicy.MaxDelay
- [ ] CloseAsync with a very large CloseHandshakeTimeout does not throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException after state change

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketConnectionOptions validation couples MaxMessageSize, MaxFrameSize and FragmentationThreshold and keeps single-valued parameters
body:
## Summary
Setting MaxMessageSize alone below MaxFrameSize fails Validate with a message naming a property the caller did not touch, and FragmentationThreshold (outbound) is validated against MaxFrameSize (inbound). Extensions is a public list that must stay empty, PerMessageDeflateOptions accepts exactly one value for clientMaxWindowBits and serverNoContextTakeover, and CompressionLevel maps to different effort buckets in the two encoders.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:240`

## Problem
Validate throws 'MaxFrameSize must be <= MaxMessageSize' (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:240-241) and both default to 4 MB, so `new WebSocketConnectionOptions { MaxMessageSize = 1 MB }` is invalid until MaxFrameSize is lowered too (Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketMessageLimitTests.cs Options_Validate_RejectsMaxFrameSizeAboveMaxMessageSize pins this). FragmentationThreshold, the size of frames the client sends, is validated against MaxFrameSize, the largest frame it accepts (:237-238), so restricting inbound frames below 64 KB also forces a change to outbound fragmentation. `Extensions` is a public settable list that must stay empty and is only rejected (:89-94, 270-282). PerMessageDeflateOptions takes `clientMaxWindowBits` (must be 15) and `serverNoContextTakeover` (must be true) and throws otherwise (PerMessageDeflateOptions.cs:43-65). CompressionLevel 0-9 maps to three DeflateStream levels (0, 1-3, 4-9; PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:427-436) and to three different chain lengths in SyncFlushDeflater (1-3, 4-6, 7-9; SyncFlushDeflater.cs:112-119), so the same number means different effort depending on which encoder a message takes.

**Failure scenario.** A developer hardening a client sets only MaxMessageSize = 64 KB and gets ArgumentException at ConnectAsync naming a property they did not touch; after fixing MaxFrameSize they hit a second exception for FragmentationThreshold.

## Suggested fix
Clamp dependent defaults (effective MaxFrameSize = min(MaxFrameSize, MaxMessageSize) unless explicitly set), stop coupling FragmentationThreshold to the inbound limit, remove `Extensions` and the single-valued constructor parameters, and document the real compression-level buckets.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Lowering MaxMessageSize alone yields a valid configuration (effective MaxFrameSize is clamped) and FragmentationThreshold is not validated against the inbound limit
- [ ] The public Extensions list and single-valued compression constructor parameters are removed or made meaningful
- [ ] CompressionLevel buckets are documented and consistent across both encoders
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ sets only MaxMessageSize = 1 MB and asserts Validate and connect succeed and fails before the fix

title: [WebSocket] Default MaxFragmentCount of 64 closes connections with 1009 for messages far below MaxMessageSize
body:
## Summary
The MessageAssembler fails the connection with close code 1009 at the 65th fragment regardless of accumulated size, which is already bounded by MaxMessageSize. Servers that write messages through a small fixed frame buffer (Tomcat/Spring Boot, 8 KiB) send a 600 KB message as about 74 frames and are rejected although MaxMessageSize is 4 MB. The Autobahn harness has to raise the option to 70000 and the documentation does not mention it.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConstants.cs:26`

## Problem
DefaultMaxFragmentCount = 64 (WebSocketConstants.cs:26) feeds the MessageAssembler (WebSocketConnection.cs:173). TryStageFragment throws ProtocolViolation with close code 1009 when _fragmentCount + 1 > _maxFragmentCount (MessageAssembler.cs:155-164) whatever the accumulated size, although the size is already bounded by MaxMessageSize (181-189). Tools~/autobahn/Program.cs:73 has to raise MaxFragmentCount to 70000 for the 9.3/9.4 cases and the README says the defaults 'would close those 9.x cases with 1009 by design'. Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md 'Message size limits' (119-124) does not mention the option.

**Failure scenario.** A server that writes text messages through a fixed 8 KiB frame buffer (Tomcat's WsRemoteEndpoint, so Spring Boot's default) sends a 600 KB JSON message as about 74 frames. The client fails the connection with 1009 at the 65th fragment although MaxMessageSize is 4 MB. Any peer that sends more than 64 frames per message is affected (4 KiB frames: 256 KB).

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 5.4

## Suggested fix
Size the fragment bound for what it protects (a default in the thousands, or a bound on empty/tiny fragments only), or append fragments into one growing pooled buffer so the count needs no tight limit. Document the option next to MaxMessageSize.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The default fragment bound no longer rejects a valid 4 MB message sent in 8 KiB frames; the bound protects against empty or tiny fragment floods without limiting normal fragmentation
- [ ] MaxFragmentCount is documented next to MaxMessageSize in Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ feeds a 600 KB message in 8 KiB fragments and asserts it is delivered, and that a flood of empty fragments is still rejected and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-protocol-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: DefaultMaxFragmentCount = 64 (WebSocketConstants.cs:26) is the option default (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:27) and feeds the assembler (WebSocketConnection.cs:173). TryStageFragment throws ProtocolViolation with close code MessageTooBig when the 65th fragment arrives, before and independent of the size check (MessageAssembler.cs:155-164 vs :181-189). Validate only requires MaxMessageSize <= MaxFrameSize * MaxFragmentCount (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:243-245), which the defaults satisfy, so nothing warns. The autobahn harness has to raise the option to 70000 (Tools~/autobahn/Program.cs:73, README.md:45-48 'by design'), and Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:119-124 does not mention the option. The limit is a deliberate phase-18 choice ('bounds metadata overhead', Development~/docs/phases/phase18/overview.md:123), but its reasoning does not hold as a default: the byte bound already caps memory, and any peer that fragments at a small fixed frame size fails at 64 x frameSize (8 KiB frames: 512 KiB) although MaxMessageSize is 4 MB. RFC 6455 5.4 puts no bound on fragment count. That Tomcat fragments text at 8 KiB is from general knowledge, not verified in this repo.

title: [WebSocket] About twenty internal plumbing types and two non-UHttpException exception types are public and would be frozen by the 1.0 API
body:
## Summary
Frame reader/writer, assembler, handshake and extension negotiation types are public but used only inside the assembly. WebSocketProtocolException and WebSocketHandshakeException derive from Exception rather than UHttpException, against the package error model. WebSocketFrameWriter has unused public methods, WebSocketClient is unsealed with no virtual members, and over 200 public members lack XML docs.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketFrameReader.cs:15`

## Problem
Public but used only inside the assembly (rg finds no reference from other Runtime assemblies, Samples~ or Documentation~; tests have InternalsVisibleTo): WebSocketFrameReader, WebSocketFrameReadLease, WebSocketFrameWriter, WebSocketFrame, MessageAssembler, WebSocketAssembledMessage, WebSocketHandshake, WebSocketHandshakeRequest, WebSocketHandshakeValidator, WebSocketHandshakeResult, WebSocketExtensionNegotiator, WebSocketExtensionNegotiationResult, WebSocketConstants (ComputeAcceptKey, GenerateClientKey, EnsureSha1Available), and arguably WebSocketConnection itself. WebSocketProtocolException (WebSocketConstants.cs:277) and WebSocketHandshakeException (WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:79) derive from Exception, not UHttpException, and are thrown by these public types (for example WebSocketHandshakeResult.ThrowIfFailed, :70-76; WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteCloseAsync, WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:141-144). WebSocketFrameWriter carries a public surface the library itself never calls (WriteTextAsync, WriteBinaryAsync, WritePingAsync, WritePongAsync, WriteMessageAsync). WebSocketClient is the only unsealed client type and has no virtual members. A rough count finds over 200 public members in the module without XML documentation, including every public member of WebSocketConnection, both client classes' constructors and Create, IWebSocketExtension, IWebSocketTransport.ConnectAsync, WebSocketTransportFactory and most WebSocketConnectionOptions/WebSocketProxySettings/WebSocketReconnectPolicy members.

**Failure scenario.** After 1.0 any change to frame buffering, the handshake result shape or the assembler (for example streaming large messages, or moving the handshake behind the transport) is a breaking change; a caller using the public reader/validator directly gets exceptions that `catch (UHttpException)` does not see, against the package error model.

## Suggested fix
Make the plumbing internal before the API freeze (tests already see internals), keep public only the client, options, message, extension, serializer and transport contracts, give the two exception types a UHttpException base or make them internal, seal WebSocketClient, and document what stays public.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Plumbing types are internal; only client, options, message, extension, serializer and transport contracts remain public
- [ ] WebSocketProtocolException and WebSocketHandshakeException derive from UHttpException or are internal, and WebSocketClient is sealed
- [ ] Remaining public members have XML documentation
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ or an API-surface check asserts the public type list of the WebSocket assembly and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-17` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Verified. Public and unreferenced outside TurboHTTP.WebSocket (rg over Runtime/ other assemblies, Editor/, Samples~ and Documentation~ finds no use; tests have InternalsVisibleTo, Runtime/WebSocket/AssemblyInfo.cs:3): WebSocketFrameReader (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:15), WebSocketFrameReadLease (:339), WebSocketFrameWriter (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:16), WebSocketFrame (WebSocketFrame.cs:39), MessageAssembler and WebSocketAssembledMessage (MessageAssembler.cs:11, :291), WebSocketHandshake/WebSocketHandshakeRequest (WebSocketHandshake.cs:53, :15), WebSocketHandshakeValidator/Result (WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:112, :17), WebSocketExtensionNegotiator/Result (WebSocketExtensionNegotiator.cs:9, :188), WebSocketConstants (WebSocketConstants.cs:10) and WebSocketConnection. WebSocketProtocolException (WebSocketConstants.cs:277) and WebSocketHandshakeException (WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:79) derive from Exception while WebSocketException derives from UHttpException (WebSocketException.cs:9); the connection maps both internally (WebSocketConnection.cs:327-337, SendReceive.cs:330-333), so they escape only to callers of the public plumbing (e.g. WebSocketHandshakeResult.ThrowIfFailed :70-76, WebSocketFrameWriter.WriteCloseAsync :139-144). WriteTextAsync/WriteBinaryAsync/WritePingAsync/WritePongAsync/WriteMessageAsync have no runtime caller. WebSocketClient is unsealed with no virtual or protected member (WebSocketClient.cs:12). A rough count gives about 310 public declarations without a preceding XML doc comment in the two assemblies (some are members of internal types or interface implementations), so 'over 200' is fair; CLAUDE.md section 4 requires XML docs and 'prefer internal'. No open issue covers the WebSocket public surface (#76 is Core InternalsVisibleTo, #104 the experimental/GA decision, #121 a v1.2 ergonomics review). No runtime failure today; the cost is the 1.0 API freeze.

title: [WebSocket] Each received frame allocates a lease object, an assembled-message object and a header buffer in addition to WebSocketMessage
body:
## Summary
The frame reader rents a 14-byte header buffer per frame, allocates a WebSocketFrameReadLease and a Task, and the assembler allocates a WebSocketAssembledMessage before the receive loop allocates the WebSocketMessage. Lease and assembled message only carry buffer, length, opcode and RSV bits, so every unfragmented message costs three heap objects where one is needed.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketFrameReader.cs:83`

## Problem
Per received frame the reader rents and returns a 14-byte header buffer (:83, :285) although it has one caller at a time, and allocates a WebSocketFrameReadLease (:253, :268) and a Task<WebSocketFrameReadLease>; the assembler then allocates a WebSocketAssembledMessage for it (MessageAssembler.cs:254, :235) before the receive loop allocates the WebSocketMessage (WebSocketConnection.SendReceive.cs:295). Lease and assembled message are pure carriers for buffer, length, opcode and RSV bits.

**Failure scenario.** Every unfragmented message costs three heap objects plus async boxes and a pool round trip where one object is needed; at 1000 messages per second that is several thousand short-lived allocations per second on a path CLAUDE.md wants allocation-free.

## Suggested fix
Keep the header bytes in a reader-owned field, return the frame as a struct (or reuse one lease per reader), and let the assembler hand back buffer and length through out parameters.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Header bytes are kept in a reader-owned field and frames are returned as a struct or a reused lease
- [ ] The assembler hands back buffer and length without a per-message carrier object
- [ ] Allocations per unfragmented received message are reduced to the WebSocketMessage and its payload buffer, measured by an allocation test
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ asserts the per-message allocation count and fails before the fix

## Context

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [WebSocket] The frame reader has no receive buffer, so every frame costs two or three separate stream reads
body:
## Summary
WebSocketFrameReader.ReadAsync reads the 2-byte header, the length bytes and the payload with separate ReadExactAsync calls directly on the raw network or TLS stream, each at least one async stream read. Frames that arrive several per TCP segment cause thousands of socket reads per second and async state-machine allocations, against the platform guidance that hot read paths complete synchronously from buffered data.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketFrameReader.cs:88`

## Problem
WebSocketFrameReader.ReadAsync reads straight from the connection stream with ReadExactAsync: 2 header bytes (:88), then 2 or 8 length bytes (:134, :143), then the payload (:239); each is at least one stream.ReadAsync (:299). The stream is the raw HoldingNetworkStream or the TLS stream returned by RawSocketWebSocketTransport (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:142, :236); no buffered reader sits in between (WebSocketConnection.cs:193, :284-287). ReadExactAsync is async Task<bool> and ReadAsync async Task<lease>, so each call that does not complete synchronously boxes a state machine and allocates a Task; platform.md asks hot ReadAsync paths to complete synchronously from buffered data.

**Failure scenario.** A server pushes 1000 small frames per second that arrive several per TCP segment: the client issues 2000-3000 socket reads per second (recv syscalls on ws://, SslStream reads on wss://), each with its async allocations on Mono/IL2CPP, instead of one read per segment. CPU, GC pressure and per-message latency scale with frame count instead of bytes.

## Suggested fix
Give the reader a pooled receive buffer (8-16 KB) owned by the receive loop: fill it with one ReadAsync, parse headers and small payloads from it synchronously, and read only large payloads directly into the payload buffer.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The reader uses a pooled receive buffer (8-16 KB) owned by the receive loop, filled by one ReadAsync and parsed synchronously for headers and small payloads
- [ ] Large payloads are read directly into the payload buffer
- [ ] Stream reads per frame for small frames arriving in one segment drop to at most one per segment, measured by a counting stream
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ uses a counting stream and asserts the read count for a batch of small frames and fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described. WebSocketFrameReader.ReadAsync issues ReadExactAsync for 2 header bytes (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:88), then 2 or 8 length bytes (:134, :143), then the payload (:239), each at least one stream.ReadAsync (:299) directly on the connection stream; the only wrapper is PrefetchedStream for bytes left over from the handshake (WebSocketConnection.cs:284-287). The stream is the raw HoldingNetworkStream or the TLS stream (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:142, :236, :243), and HoldingNetworkStream.ReadAsync forwards to NetworkStream with no buffering (HoldingNetworkStream.cs:58-71). ReadExactAsync is async Task<bool> and ReadAsync async Task<lease>, against the guidance in Development~/docs/agents/platform.md:43-44. So a frame costs 1 read (empty), 2 (<=125 bytes) or 3 (longer). Caveat: on wss:// the TLS stream serves the small reads from its decrypted record buffer, so the extra socket reads apply to ws:// and the per-read task/state-machine allocations to both; the magnitude is not measured. No open issue covers the WebSocket receive path (#120, #416, #434 are HTTP body paths).

Related: [[R11-ws-runtime-24]].

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketFrameReader accepts non-minimal 16-bit and 64-bit payload length encodings
body:
## Summary
WebSocketFrameReader decodes the 126 and 127 length forms without checking that the value needed the longer form. A server can send a 5-byte payload in the 16-bit or 64-bit form and the message is delivered. RFC 6455 requires the minimal encoding, so the connection must fail with 1002.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketFrameReader.cs:132`

## Problem
The 126 branch reads a 16-bit length and the 127 branch a 64-bit length (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:132-157); only the most significant bit of the 64-bit form is checked (149). Nothing rejects a 16-bit length below 126 or a 64-bit length of 65535 or less. No test covers it (no 'minimal' match under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket).

**Failure scenario.** A server sends 0x81 0x7E 0x00 0x05 'hello' (a 5-byte payload in the 16-bit form) or the 64-bit form with length 5. The message is delivered normally instead of failing the connection with 1002.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 5.2

## Suggested fix
After decoding, throw WebSocketProtocolException(InvalidFrame) when the 16-bit form carries less than 126 or the 64-bit form carries 0xFFFF or less.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A frame using the 16-bit length form with a value below 126, or the 64-bit form with a value of 0xFFFF or less, fails the connection with WebSocketProtocolException(InvalidFrame) and close code 1002
- [ ] Minimal encodings (125, 126, 65535, 65536) still parse
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketFrameWriter issues a separate header write and one write per 8 KB chunk for frames above 8 KB
body:
## Summary
For frames larger than the 8 KB masking buffer, WebSocketFrameWriter writes the header alone and then one stream write per 8 KB chunk. A 1 MB message with the default 64 KB fragmentation threshold produces 144 stream writes, each a syscall on ws:// or a TLS record on wss://. Mobile and high-throughput senders pay for this in CPU and allocations.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:300`

## Problem
WriteFrameAsync coalesces header and payload only when both fit the 8 KB masking buffer (TryWriteSmallFrameSingleWriteAsync, :337-359; DefaultMaskingChunkSize :18). Larger frames write the 6-14 byte header alone (:300) and then one stream write per 8 KB chunk (:315-335), followed by FlushAsync (:304). The connection never passes a larger chunk size (WebSocketConnection.cs:172) and the socket has NoDelay set (Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:491).

**Failure scenario.** A 1 MB message with the default 64 KB fragmentation threshold becomes 16 frames x (1 header write + 8 chunk writes) = 144 stream writes: 144 send syscalls on ws:// (each header its own TCP segment) or 144 TLS records on wss://, each with its Task and state-machine allocations, where 16 to 32 writes would do.

## Suggested fix
Put the header in front of the first chunk and size the masking buffer to the fragmentation threshold (pooled, capped) so that a fragment is one write.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The header is written together with the first payload chunk, and a fragment up to the fragmentation threshold is sent in one stream write using a pooled, capped masking buffer
- [ ] Sending a 1 MB message with the default 64 KB threshold performs at most 32 stream writes (counted with a recording stream), down from 144
- [ ] Pooled buffers are returned once on success, exception and cancellation
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WriteFrameAsync (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:294-304) coalesces only when header+payload <= _maskingChunkBuffer.Length (TryWriteSmallFrameSingleWriteAsync :347-349); otherwise it writes the header alone (:300), then one stream.WriteAsync per 8 KiB chunk (:325-334), then FlushAsync (:304). The connection builds the writer with the default chunk size (WebSocketConnection.cs:171 new WebSocketFrameWriter(options.FragmentationThreshold)) and writes each fragment through writer.WriteFrameAsync (SendReceive.cs:894). Default fragmentation threshold is 64 KiB (WebSocketConstants.cs:27), so a 1 MiB message is 16 frames x (1 + 8) = 144 writes. The stream is HoldingNetworkStream or the TLS stream (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:142, 236), no buffering layer; sockets have NoDelay (HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:490-493). No guard found, no open issue.

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketFrameWriter.ApplyMaskInPlace masks one byte per iteration through a four-way switch
body:
## Summary
Outbound masking XORs each payload byte separately through a switch on the key index, with bounds checks per byte. Every outbound payload byte goes through it, on the sending thread, which can be the Unity main thread. Word-at-a-time masking without unsafe code is much cheaper on ARM64 IL2CPP.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:425`

## Problem
WebSocketFrameWriter.ApplyMaskInPlace (:413-444) masks one byte per iteration through a switch on (payloadOffset + i) & 3, with array bounds checks per byte; it is applied to every outbound payload byte (:330, :355). WebSocketFrameReader.ApplyMask (WebSocketFrameReader.cs:319-333) is also bytewise but only runs for masked server frames, which the client rejects.

**Failure scenario.** Sending a 1 MB binary message runs one million switch iterations on the sending thread (the Unity main thread for the first chunk when SendAsync is called from it). Word-at-a-time masking needs no unsafe code and is roughly an order of magnitude cheaper on ARM64 IL2CPP.

## Suggested fix
Rotate the 4-byte key by payloadOffset & 3, XOR 8 bytes at a time through MemoryMarshal.Cast<byte, ulong> (or BinaryPrimitives), and finish the tail bytewise.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ApplyMaskInPlace XORs 8 bytes at a time (rotated key, MemoryMarshal.Cast or BinaryPrimitives) and handles the tail bytewise, without unsafe code
- [ ] Output is byte-identical to the current implementation for all payload offsets and lengths 0 to 64 and for a 1 MB payload
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it
- [ ] Masking a 1 MB payload is measurably faster than the bytewise version in a recorded benchmark

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-runtime-10` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: WebSocketFrameWriter.ApplyMaskInPlace (WebSocketFrameWriter.cs:413-444) XORs one byte per iteration through a switch on (payloadOffset + i) & 3, and it is the only masking path for every outbound payload byte (:330 chunked path, :355 small-frame path). No vectorised/word path exists and nothing upstream masks. No open issue. Downgraded to low: cost is linear and real but small next to TLS (especially BouncyCastle) on the same bytes, and typical WebSocket payloads are small; the 'order of magnitude' gain on ARM64 IL2CPP is an unmeasured estimate.

Related: [[R11-ws-runtime-11]].

title: [WebSocket] Handshake custom-header validation accepts non-token names and control characters in values
body:
## Summary
ValidateCustomHeader rejects only CR, LF and ':' in names and CR/LF or non-ASCII in values. Names with spaces and values with NUL or other control characters are written raw into the upgrade request. A leading-space name becomes an obs-fold continuation of the previous header, and 'Host ' emits a second Host field. Apps that build CustomHeaders from configuration or user input are exposed to header smuggling toward lenient servers and intermediaries.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshake.cs:273`

## Problem
ValidateCustomHeader (WebSocketHandshake.cs:273-305) rejects only CR, LF and ':' in names, CR/LF in values and non-ASCII; names such as " X", "X Y", "Host " and values with NUL, 0x01-0x1F or 0x7F pass and are appended raw (143-146). HttpHeaders.Add does not validate (Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:49-64). The reserved-name check is an exact match (135), so "Host " or " Sec-WebSocket-Key" passes it, and Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding are not reserved. The HTTP path uses HttpFieldValidator.ValidateField (Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:517).

**Failure scenario.** An app builds CustomHeaders from configuration or user input. A name with a leading space is emitted as an obs-fold continuation of the previous header line (for example appended to Sec-WebSocket-Extensions), "Host " emits a second Host field with whitespace before the colon, and a value with NUL goes on the wire. Lenient servers and intermediaries parse these differently from what the client intended, a header-confusion surface the HTTP stack already closes.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 5.1, 5.5; RFC 9112 5.1

## Suggested fix
Apply the HttpFieldValidator rules (token names, VCHAR/SP/HTAB values without surrounding whitespace) in ValidateCustomHeader; the validator lives in Transport, so move the rule to Core.Internal or duplicate the small check. Add Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding to the reserved names.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Custom header names must be RFC 9110 tokens and values must be VCHAR/SP/HTAB without leading or trailing whitespace; violations throw before anything is sent
- [ ] Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding are added to the reserved header names, with a case-insensitive check
- [ ] The check lives in Core.Internal or is a small duplicate in the WebSocket module, with no new module reference
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [WebSocket] An interim 1xx response before 101 fails the opening handshake with HandshakeFailed
body:
## Summary
WebSocketHandshakeValidator reads one response head and fails for any status other than 101. A 100 Continue or 103 Early Hints before the 101 is treated as a failed handshake, and the resilient client retries it on every attempt. RFC 9110 allows interim responses before the final one.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:178`

## Problem
ValidateAsync reads one response head and returns a failure for any status other than 101 (WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:178-196). 100, 102 and 103 are not skipped; ResponseCanHaveBody (639-643) only suppresses the body read for them.

**Failure scenario.** A server or intermediary answers 'HTTP/1.1 103 Early Hints' (or 100 Continue) followed by '101 Switching Protocols'. ConnectAsync throws HandshakeFailed with status 103, and the resilient client treats it as transient and repeats it on every attempt.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 15.2; RFC 6455 4.1

## Suggested fix
Loop over interim responses: for a 1xx other than 101 discard the head and parse the next one from the trailing bytes and the stream, within the same byte budget and a small count limit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Interim 1xx responses other than 101 are discarded and the next head is parsed from the trailing bytes and the stream, within the same byte budget and a small count limit (for example 8)
- [ ] A 103 followed by 101 completes the handshake; more interim responses than the limit fails with HandshakeFailed
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketHandshakeValidator is a third hand-written HTTP/1.1 response parser with rules differing from the transport's
body:
## Summary
The WebSocket module may reference only Core, so the opening handshake carries its own status-line, header, Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding and chunked parsing, about 600 lines next to Http11ResponseParser. The two parsers accept different inputs and use different size limits, and the WebSocket one has a fixed header limit with no option. Each parser hardening has to be made twice.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:358`

## Problem
Because TurboHTTP.WebSocket may reference only Core, the opening handshake carries its own status-line/header parser (TryParseHttpResponse, :358-414), Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding framing (:645-729) and chunked reader (:751-801), about 600 of the file's 940 lines, next to Http11ResponseParser and ConnectReplyReader in Runtime/Transport/Http1. The rules have diverged: the validator trims the field name (`line.Substring(0, colon).Trim()`, :401) so `Sec-WebSocket-Accept : x` and a whitespace-led continuation line are accepted as fields, while Http11ResponseParser rejects whitespace before the colon and obs-fold (Http11ResponseParser.cs:694-713); the validator caps the whole head at 8 KiB with no per-line limit (:114, :279-283) and is not configurable from WebSocketConnectionOptions (the error text says 'configured size limit'), while ConnectReplyReader uses 8 KiB per line and 16 KiB per block (ConnectReplyReader.cs:73-76); the validator decodes ASCII and splits on CRLF only. WebSocket.Transport already references Transport and could host the handshake I/O.

**Failure scenario.** A 101 response with a 9 KiB header block (large Set-Cookie from a gateway) is accepted by an HTTPS request to the same origin but fails the WebSocket handshake with 'headers exceeded the configured size limit' and no option to raise it; a malformed head the HTTP parser rejects is accepted by the WebSocket path. Every future parser hardening has to be made three times.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 5.1, 5.2

## Suggested fix
Put one bounded response-head reader where both stacks can use it (Core.Internal, or perform the upgrade exchange in TurboHTTP.WebSocket.Transport using the transport's reader) and keep only the RFC 6455 checks (Upgrade/Connection/Accept/subprotocol/extensions) in the WebSocket module; surface the header limit as an option.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One bounded response-head reader is shared by both stacks (Core.Internal, or the upgrade exchange moves to TurboHTTP.WebSocket.Transport), and the WebSocket module keeps only the RFC 6455 checks
- [ ] The handshake rejects the same malformed heads as Http11ResponseParser (whitespace before the colon, non-token names, obs-fold)
- [ ] The maximum handshake header size is exposed as a WebSocketConnectionOptions value
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `ws-design-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/ws.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WebSocketHandshakeValidator has its own head parser (TryParseHttpResponse :358-414): ASCII decode, split on CRLF, name = Substring(0, colon).Trim() (:401), no token check (HttpHeaders.Add only rejects blank names, HttpHeaders.cs:49-64). Http11ResponseParser rejects a whitespace-led line, whitespace before the colon and non-token names (Http11ResponseParser.cs:694-713). Head cap is 8 KiB total (DefaultMaxResponseHeaderBytes :114, enforced :279-283) and WebSocketConnection calls ValidateAsync without the limit arguments (WebSocketConnection.cs:219-222), with no option on WebSocketConnectionOptions; the HTTP parser allows 8192 per line and 100 KB total (Http11ResponseParser.cs:156-158), ConnectReplyReader 8 KiB/16 KiB (ConnectReplyReader.cs:73-76). Corrections: a whitespace-led line is accepted as a field only when it contains a colon (otherwise 'Malformed response header line', :393-397); RFC 9112 5.1 does not oblige a client to reject whitespace before the colon in a response, so this is divergence and duplication, not a protocol violation. #187 (fold WebSocket.Transport into Transport) is adjacent but does not track the duplicated parser or the fixed limit.

Related: #187, [[R11-ws-protocol-09]], [[R11-ws-protocol-11]].

title: [WebSocket] ConnectionQuality is relative to the connection's first three RTT samples and does not describe link quality
body:
## Summary
ComputeQuality scores against a baseline taken from the first three RTT samples of the same connection, plus a loss term that is near zero because a missed pong ends the connection. A connection opened on a slow link with a steady 2 s round trip reports Excellent for its life, and Critical is practically unreachable. UI driven by the quality event misleads users.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHealthMonitor.cs:197`

## Problem
ComputeQuality_NoLock returns Unknown until three RTT samples exist, then scores `0.6 * clamp(baseline / average) + 0.4 * (1 - (pings - pongs) / pings)` (WebSocketHealthMonitor.cs:197-220) where the baseline is the mean of the first three samples of this connection (:102-115). A missed pong ends the connection through PongTimeout (SendReceive.cs:1002-1016), so `pings - pongs` is 0 or transiently 1 and the loss term stays about 0.4. With the default 25 s PingInterval the first verdict arrives after about 75 s. The weights and thresholds (0.6, 0.4, 0.9/0.7/0.5/0.3) are unnamed literals. IWebSocketClient.OnConnectionQualityChanged documents the event as 'physical connection quality ... (e.g. Good to Poor)' (IWebSocketClient.cs:47).

**Failure scenario.** A connection opened on a poor cellular link with a steady 2 s round trip reports Excellent for its whole life; a connection whose RTT rises from 5 ms to 15 ms on Wi-Fi drops to Fair (0.6 x 0.33 + 0.4 = 0.6); Critical is unreachable in practice because with the loss term pinned near 0.4 the score cannot fall below 0.4. UI driven by the event misleads users.

## Suggested fix
Score against absolute RTT/jitter bands (configurable) with the relative trend as a secondary input, drop or redefine the loss term, name the constants, and document the meaning of each band.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Quality is scored against absolute RTT and jitter bands (configurable) with the relative trend as a secondary input
- [ ] The loss term is redefined or removed, constants are named, and each band is documented in XML docs
- [ ] A steady 2 s RTT does not report Excellent, and a sustained RTT increase reaches Poor or Critical

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketMessage.Dispose is not atomic and a concurrent double dispose returns the same array to the pool twice
body:
## Summary
Dispose reads _buffer, nulls it and returns the array to the shared ByteArrayPool without interlocking. Two threads disposing the same message can both return the array. The pool then hands one array to two renters, so later WebSocket messages or HTTP body buffers overwrite each other.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketMessage.cs:70`

## Problem
WebSocketMessage.Dispose (:70-81) reads _buffer, nulls it and returns the array to ByteArrayPool with no interlocking; the type is handed to user code from ReceiveAsync/ReceiveAllAsync with returnToPool true. ByteArrayPool is the process-wide ArrayPool<byte>.Shared facade used by the HTTP stack as well (Runtime/Core/Internal/ByteArrayPool.cs:56).

**Failure scenario.** Two threads dispose the same pull-mode message (a consumer's using on one thread, cleanup on another): both see a non-null _buffer and return the array twice; the pool then hands the same array to two renters, so two later messages or an HTTP body buffer overwrite each other.

## Suggested fix
Claim the buffer with Interlocked.Exchange(ref _buffer, null) before returning it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dispose claims the buffer with Interlocked.Exchange(ref _buffer, null) and returns it to the pool at most once
- [ ] Concurrent Dispose calls from multiple threads return the array exactly once, and later access to a disposed message behaves as before

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketMetricsCollector takes its lock three to four times and reads two clocks per message in each direction
body:
## Summary
The always-on collector locks separately in RecordFrameReceived, RecordMessageReceived and ShouldPublishSnapshot, and reads Stopwatch and DateTimeOffset.UtcNow several times per message. At thousands of messages per second this adds lock traffic and clock reads for counters most applications never read.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketMetricsCollector.cs:147`

## Problem
Receiving one message takes the collector lock in RecordFrameReceived (:62-72), RecordMessageReceived (:98-106) and ShouldPublishSnapshot (:147-163), plus RecordCompressedInboundBytes when compressed (:120-127); each reads Stopwatch. TouchActivity adds DateTimeOffset.UtcNow and three Interlocked exchanges per frame and per message (WebSocketConnection.Lifecycle.cs:331-341). The send side mirrors this (WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:64-70) on the same lock, shared with the receive loop. The collector is created unconditionally (WebSocketConnection.cs:272).

**Failure scenario.** At a few thousand messages per second the sender and the receive loop each take the same monitor 3-4 times per message and read two clocks, for counters most applications never look at.

## Suggested fix
Fold the per-message updates and the publish decision into one locked call (or Interlocked counters with a single timestamp).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Per-message updates and the snapshot-publish decision happen in one locked call or with Interlocked counters and a single timestamp read
- [ ] Metric values (counts, bytes, rates, snapshot publishing) are unchanged for existing metrics tests
- [ ] Lock acquisitions per received message drop from 3-4 to 1, shown by a test or benchmark

title: [WebSocket] WebSocketProxySettings re-implements proxy settings and bypass matching with different rules than Core's ProxySettings
body:
## Summary
WebSocketProxySettings supports only exact and '*.domain' bypass rules, while Core's ProxySettings and ProxyBypassMatcher also support '.domain', CIDR, ports and bracketed IPv6. The same BypassList therefore routes the same host differently for HTTP and WebSocket, and client.WebSocket(uri) ignores the client's proxy. WebSocket traffic can go through a proxy that the app configured to bypass.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketProxySettings.cs:82`

## Problem
Core has public ProxySettings (Address, NetworkCredential Credentials, BypassList, UseEnvironmentVariables, AllowPlaintextProxyAuth) and public ProxyBypassMatcher.IsBypassed (Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:9-157), whose documented rules include `.example.com` (apex plus subdomains), CIDR, an optional `:port` and bracketed IPv6. WebSocket, which references Core, defines its own WebSocketProxySettings (ProxyUri, ProxyCredentials struct, BypassList) with ShouldBypass supporting only exact names and `*.domain` (WebSocketProxySettings.cs:82-112); a bracketed IPv6 rule is compared as written (comment at :125-127) against a host the transport already stripped of brackets (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:355-361, 85), so `[::1]` never matches. Environment proxies (HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY) are not consulted, Basic-over-cleartext consent reuses AllowCleartext instead of AllowPlaintextProxyAuth (ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:110-116), and UnityWebSocketExtensions.BuildWebSocketOptions copies TlsBackend, AllowCleartext and headers from the UHttpClient but cannot copy its proxy because the types differ.

**Failure scenario.** A project configures the HTTP client with BypassList { ".corp.example", "10.0.0.0/8" }. The same list given to WebSocketProxySettings matches neither ws://api.corp.example nor ws://10.1.2.3, so those sockets are sent through the proxy (or fail there) while HTTP requests to the same hosts go direct; `client.WebSocket(uri)` ignores the client's proxy entirely.

## Suggested fix
Accept Core's ProxySettings on WebSocketConnectionOptions (or make WebSocketProxySettings a thin adapter) and call ProxyBypassMatcher.IsBypassed(host, port, rules) so both stacks share one rule grammar, credential type and consent flag; then let the Unity extension carry the HTTP client's proxy over.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WebSocketConnectionOptions accepts Core's ProxySettings (or WebSocketProxySettings becomes an adapter) and calls ProxyBypassMatcher.IsBypassed so both stacks share one rule grammar, credential type and plaintext-auth consent flag
- [ ] A BypassList of '.corp.example' and '10.0.0.0/8' bypasses ws://api.corp.example and ws://10.1.2.3
- [ ] The Unity client extension carries the HTTP client's proxy over to client.WebSocket(uri)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it

Verifier note: Traced. Core exposes public ProxySettings and ProxyBypassMatcher.IsBypassed with '.domain', CIDR, ':port' and bracket-insensitive IPv6 rules (Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:9-31, 69-157). WebSocketProxySettings.ShouldBypass supports only exact match and '*.domain' (WebSocketProxySettings.cs:82-112); rules keep their brackets (comment :125-127) while the transport passes a bracket-stripped host (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:78, 85, 355-361), so a '[::1]' rule never matches (a bare '::1' rule does). No environment-proxy lookup exists in the WebSocket path, Basic-over-cleartext consent is options.AllowCleartext (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:199, ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:108-116), and UnityWebSocketExtensions.BuildWebSocketOptions copies TlsBackend, AllowCleartext and headers only (UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:44-54). title: [WebSocket] The default reconnect predicate ignores close codes 1012 Service Restart and 1013 Try Again Later
body:
## Summary
DefaultReconnectOnCloseCode returns true only for 1001, 1006 and 1011, while the validator accepts 1012 to 1014 from the peer. A server deploy that closes clients with 1012 or 1013 stops ResilientWebSocketClient after OnClosed, although 1001 from the same deploy would reconnect. Both codes are registered as retryable conditions.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketReconnectPolicy.cs:129`

## Problem
DefaultReconnectOnCloseCode returns true only for 1001, 1006 and 1011 (WebSocketReconnectPolicy.cs:129-134). ValidateCloseCode accepts 1012-1014 from the peer (WebSocketConstants.cs:92-109), so they reach the policy through ShouldReconnect (112-127).

**Failure scenario.** A server deploy closes all clients with 1012 Service Restart (or 1013 Try Again Later). ResilientWebSocketClient raises OnClosed and stops, where 1001 from the same deploy would have reconnected.

## Spec reference
RFC 6455 11.7 (IANA close code registry)

## Suggested fix
Include 1012 and 1013 in the default predicate (with the normal backoff); keep 1000, 1002, 1003 and 1007-1010 terminal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The default predicate returns true for 1012 and 1013, with the normal backoff
- [ ] 1000, 1002, 1003 and 1007 to 1010 stay terminal

title: [WebSocket] IWebSocketTransport sits behind a single-slot static factory with implicit stream contract and needless ownership tracking
body:
## Summary
IWebSocketTransport only opens a byte stream, and its one production implementation holds no resources, yet WebSocketClient tracks ownership and disposal of a fresh instance in four places. The static factory has one slot, so a custom registration can be overwritten by the next bootstrap, for example with Enter Play Mode without domain reload. The stream contract is not documented, and the WebGL extension point is unclear.

## Location
- `Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketTransportFactory.cs:14`

## Problem
IWebSocketTransport.ConnectAsync returns a Stream after TCP/TLS (IWebSocketTransport.cs:12-18); its only production implementation is RawSocketWebSocketTransport, whose Dispose just sets a flag (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:281-284), yet WebSocketClient tracks ownership and disposal of a fresh instance per connect in four places (WebSocketClient.cs:140-141, 167-178, 353, 668-676). The connection depends on undocumented stream behaviour: Dispose must fault a pending read (#226, WebSocketConnection.cs:195-200), one reader and one writer run concurrently, and cancellation tokens may be ignored. Because the contract is a raw byte stream, a browser WebSocket (the only alternative a WebGL build could use) cannot implement it, so on WebGL the module compiles (the asmdef has no platform exclusion) and fails at the factory with InvalidOperationException. WebSocketTransportFactory holds one process-wide delegate (WebSocketTransportFactory.cs:11-23): RawSocketWebSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered replaces whatever is registered (RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:52-56), and it runs from the bootstrap on every play-mode entry and from the module initializer whenever a runtime fires it; Reset is internal here but public on HttpTransportFactory.

**Failure scenario.** A project registers a custom WebSocket factory once (static constructor or [InitializeOnLoadMethod]); with Enter Play Mode without domain reload the next session's bootstrap overwrites it and new clients silently use the raw-socket transport. Whether a late module initializer does the same depends on the runtime (confirm on a player where module initializers run).

## Suggested fix
Document the stream contract on the interface, keep a separate 'default' and 'override' slot in the factory (EnsureRegistered sets only the default), drop per-client ownership of stateless transports, and decide whether the WebGL extension point is IWebSocketClient (then exclude WebGL in the asmdef or provide a clear compile-time story).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The stream contract (read/write, cancellation, flush and disposal expectations) is documented on IWebSocketTransport
- [ ] WebSocketTransportFactory keeps separate default and override slots, and EnsureRegistered sets only the default, so a custom override survives bootstrap
- [ ] Per-client ownership of stateless transports is removed, and the WebGL extension point is decided and documented
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and passes after it
